tcz: Jan khat chun songkul insunga kihen teni Egypt lengpa juvaihompa le an vaihompa chun mang khat cheh, amang ledohna toh kilhon cheh-in anei lhon in ahi.
en_web: They both dreamed a dream, each man his dream, in one night, each man according to the interpretation of his dream, the cup bearer and the baker of the king of Egypt, who were bound in the prison.
en_kjv: And they dreamed a dream both of them, each man his dream in one night, each man according to the interpretation of his dream, the butler and the baker of the king of Egypt, which were bound in the prison.

tcz: Hichun Joseph in amani chu jingkah lama amailhon lunglhai lou chu ahedohtan Joseph in amani chu adongin, ibola nang teni namai lhon kipah lou ham ati.
en_web: Joseph came in to them in the morning, and saw them, and saw that they were sad.
en_kjv: And Joseph came in unto them in the morning, and looked upon them, and behold, they were sad.

tcz: Joseph in adong in, “Sopi teni ibola namai lhon lhailou ham,” ati.
en_web: He asked Pharaoh’s officers who were with him in custody in his master’s house, saying, “Why do you look so sad today?”
en_kjv: And he asked Pharaoh’s officers that were with him in the ward of his lord’s house, saying, Wherefore look ye so sadly to day?

tcz: Amanin adon but lhon in, “Janlhah in keinin mang kanei gel lhon in amavang koi machan kamang ipi kisei na ahi aledoh thei aumpoi ati lhon e, ahin Joseph in adonbut in,” mang in ipi ahetsah dichu Pathen kin ahi. Chule namang lhon chu neisei peh lhon in ati.
en_web: They said to him, “We have dreamed a dream, and there is no one who can interpret it.” Joseph said to them, “Don’t interpretations belong to God? Please tell it to me.”
en_kjv: And they said unto him, We have dreamed a dream, and there is no interpreter of it. And Joseph said unto them, Do not interpretations belong to God? tell me them, I pray you.

tcz: Hichun khon dom le a pang lamkai pa chun Joseph chu amang ho chu asei peh tai. Ka manga lengpi bah ka masanga ka mun.
en_web: The chief cup bearer told his dream to Joseph, and said to him, “In my dream, behold, a vine was in front of me,
en_kjv: And the chief butler told his dream to Joseph, and said to him, In my dream, behold, a vine was before me;

tcz: Hiche lengpi phunga chun abah thum ajam kamun, gang tah in ahung mum in chu in apah lha tai, hiche aga hochu lengpithei ga ahung hitai.
en_web: and in the vine were three branches. It was as though it budded, it blossomed, and its clusters produced ripe grapes.
en_kjv: and in the vine were three branches: and it was as though it budded, and her blossoms shot forth; and the clusters thereof brought forth ripe grapes:

tcz: Pharaoh chakhon chu ka khut chunga ana um'in, hichun keiman lengpi ga chu ka sujot in atwi chu Pharaoh khona ka sun peh e.
en_web: Pharaoh’s cup was in my hand; and I took the grapes, and pressed them into Pharaoh’s cup, and I gave the cup into Pharaoh’s hand.”
en_kjv: and Pharaoh’s cup was in my hand: and I took the grapes, and pressed them into Pharaoh’s cup, and I gave the cup into Pharaoh’s hand.

tcz: Joseph in hitin aseiye, “Lengpi bah thum hochu nithum tina ahi.
en_web: Joseph said to him, “This is its interpretation: the three branches are three days.
en_kjv: And Joseph said unto him, This is the interpretation of it: The three branches are three days:

tcz: Nithum sunga hi Pharaoh in nithum jou teng nadom sang intin, chule masanga nana toh na a nanung koi kit ding ahi.
en_web: Within three more days, Pharaoh will lift up your head, and restore you to your office. You will give Pharaoh’s cup into his hand, the way you did when you were his cup bearer.
en_kjv: yet within three days shall Pharaoh lift up thine head, and restore thee unto thy place: and thou shalt deliver Pharaoh’s cup into his hand, after the former manner when thou wast his butler.

tcz: Chule nangma koma katao ahi, chanvou pha nahung chan teng neihin sumil hih beh in Pharaoh koma hitobang kathil bol hohi eina seipeh in, ajeh chu songkul'a kona eilha doh thei na ding in,” ati.
en_web: But remember me when it is well with you. Please show kindness to me, and make mention of me to Pharaoh, and bring me out of this house.
en_kjv: But think on me when it shall be well with thee, and shew kindness, I pray thee, unto me, and make mention of me unto Pharaoh, and bring me out of this house:

tcz: Ajeh chu Hebrew gam a ka in apat a eikiman doh tua hiche songkul'a kaum hi mona neilou bolkhel ka neipoi.
en_web: For indeed, I was stolen away out of the land of the Hebrews, and here also I have done nothing that they should put me into the dungeon.”
en_kjv: for indeed I was stolen away out of the land of the Hebrews: and here also have I done nothing that they should put me into the dungeon.

tcz: Hichun changlhah hom'a lamkai pachu Joseph in amang hoitah a ale chu amu le ama jong atha anom lheh in; Joseph jah ah hitin aseiye, “Keiman jong jan mang kaneiye, ka manga chun paipeh thum changlhah dimset kalu chunga kapoi.
en_web: When the chief baker saw that the interpretation was good, he said to Joseph, “I also was in my dream, and behold, three baskets of white bread were on my head.
en_kjv: When the chief baker saw that the interpretation was good, he said unto Joseph, I also was in my dream, and behold, I had three white baskets on my head:

tcz: Paipeh achuna pa sunga chun changlhah ajat lhingsel in aum in, Pharaoh a ding ahi, ahin vacha ho ahung leng un ka luchunga changlhah ho chu ane doh tauve.”
en_web: In the uppermost basket there were all kinds of baked food for Pharaoh, and the birds ate them out of the basket on my head.”
en_kjv: and in the uppermost basket there was of all manner of bakemeats for Pharaoh; and the birds did eat them out of the basket upon my head.

tcz: Joseph in amang chu ale pehtan, “Paipeh thum chun nithum ma avetsah ahin,
en_web: Joseph answered, “This is its interpretation. The three baskets are three days.
en_kjv: And Joseph answered and said, This is the interpretation thereof: The three baskets are three days:

tcz: Nithum sunga hi Pharaoh in nalu adopsang ding thing phunga nakhai sang a, vachaten naphe anehchai ding'u ahi.”
en_web: Within three more days, Pharaoh will lift up your head from off you, and will hang you on a tree; and the birds will eat your flesh from off you.”
en_kjv: yet within three days shall Pharaoh lift up thy head from off thee, and shall hang thee on a tree; and the birds shall eat thy flesh from off thee.

tcz: Pharaoh in nithum jou in ama penni kipapina in anoiya a semang pachonga pang jouse akou khom in hiche a pang dinga chu juvai hom lamkai pa le an vaihom lamkaipa chu alhadoh gel in,
en_web: On the third day, which was Pharaoh’s birthday, he made a feast for all his servants, and he lifted up the head of the chief cup bearer and the head of the chief baker among his servants.
en_kjv: And it came to pass the third day, which was Pharaoh’s birthday, that he made a feast unto all his servants: and he lifted up the head of the chief butler and of the chief baker among his servants.

tcz: Ju vaihom pachu aju vaihom na ma man apansah kit'in, aman jong jukhon chu Pharaoh khut a agapetai.
en_web: He restored the chief cup bearer to his position again, and he gave the cup into Pharaoh’s hand;
en_kjv: And he restored the chief butler unto his butlership again; and he gave the cup into Pharaoh’s hand:

tcz: Ahin an vaihom lamkaipa vang chu Joseph in amani henga mang alepeh bang chun akhai lih tan ahi.
en_web: but he hanged the chief baker, as Joseph had interpreted to them.
en_kjv: but he hanged the chief baker: as Joseph had interpreted to them.

tcz: Hichun ju vaihom lamkaipan Joseph chu ageldoh tapon asumil deltai.
en_web: Yet the chief cup bearer didn’t remember Joseph, but forgot him.
en_kjv: Yet did not the chief butler remember Joseph, but forgat him.

tcz: Kum ni nungin Pharaoh in mang anei in ahile, vetan ama Nile vadung panga ana ding in ahi.
en_web: At the end of two full years, Pharaoh dreamed, and behold, he stood by the river.
en_kjv: And it came to pass at the end of two full years, that Pharaoh dreamed: and behold, he stood by the river.

tcz: Amanga chun bongchal sagi athao a thao cheh ahung kal doh un hamhing lah a chun alhaovin ahi.
en_web: Behold, seven cattle came up out of the river. They were sleek and fat, and they fed in the marsh grass.
en_kjv: And behold, there came up out of the river seven well favoured kine and fatfleshed; and they fed in a meadow.

tcz: Chujou in ama ho nunga chun bongchal sagi ma agon a gong cheh Nile vadunga kon chun ahung doh un, vadung panga bongchal sagi dangho koma chun ading uvin ahi.
en_web: Behold, seven other cattle came up after them out of the river, ugly and thin, and stood by the other cattle on the brink of the river.
en_kjv: And behold, seven other kine came up after them out of the river, ill favoured and leanfleshed; and stood by the other kine upon the brink of the river.

tcz: Hichun bongchal agong ho chun bongchal athao sagi ho chu aval lhum tauvin ahi. Hiche mang anei pet tah chun Pharaoh chu ahung khang doh tai.
en_web: The ugly and thin cattle ate up the seven sleek and fat cattle. So Pharaoh awoke.
en_kjv: And the ill favoured and leanfleshed kine did eat up the seven well favoured and fat kine. So Pharaoh awoke.

tcz: Ahin Pharaoh a imulhu kit in mang anivei na aneiyin, hiche amanga hin changphal sagi hoitah vetnom nom um phungkhat a kona hung kikhai lha amun ahi.
en_web: He slept and dreamed a second time; and behold, seven heads of grain came up on one stalk, healthy and good.
en_kjv: And he slept and dreamed the second time: and behold, seven ears of corn came up upon one stalk, rank and good.

tcz: Hichun changphal sagi amanga amu kit'in ahin hiche changphal ho chu ageo cheh chuh jeng in, solam huijin amut geo lheh jeng ahi.
en_web: Behold, seven heads of grain, thin and blasted with the east wind, sprung up after them.
en_kjv: And behold, seven thin ears and blasted with the east wind sprang up after them.

tcz: Chuin hiche geo chih banga changphal ho chun changphal lom sagi ahoi phungkhat a kikhai lha ho chu aval lhum kittai. Hichun Pharaoh ahung doh kit'in ahile ajan mang ahichu agel doh in ahi.
en_web: The thin heads of grain swallowed up the seven healthy and full ears. Pharaoh awoke, and behold, it was a dream.
en_kjv: And the seven thin ears devoured the seven rank and full ears. And Pharaoh awoke, and behold, it was a dream.

tcz: Hiche ni ajingkah apat'in Pharaoh chu amang ho jeh chun a suboi lheh in aum thei tapoi. Hichun Pharaoh in amaho jouse koma amang chu asei tan, ahin amaho lah a khat beh in jong ipi kiseina ham tia chu a donbut thei aum pouve.
en_web: In the morning, his spirit was troubled, and he sent and called for all of Egypt’s magicians and wise men. Pharaoh told them his dreams, but there was no one who could interpret them to Pharaoh.
en_kjv: And it came to pass in the morning that his spirit was troubled; and he sent and called for all the magicians of Egypt, and all the wise men thereof: and Pharaoh told them his dream; but there was none that could interpret them unto Pharaoh.

tcz: Phat achaina langtah chun lengpa jukhon doma lamkai pachu ahung ding doh in, “Tunia keiman geldoh khat kaneiye phat masa a kana chatvai na atin Pharaoh koma aseitan ahi.
en_web: Then the chief cup bearer spoke to Pharaoh, saying, “I remember my faults today.
en_kjv: Then spake the chief butler unto Pharaoh, saying, I do remember my faults this day:

tcz: Nangman nasoh teni chunga nana lunglhai pon changlhah hom lamkaipa le keima chunga, hijeh chun keini hi lengpa songkul'a neina koiyin ahi.
en_web: Pharaoh was angry with his servants, and put me in custody in the house of the captain of the guard, with the chief baker.
en_kjv: Pharaoh was wroth with his servants, and put me in ward in the captain of the guard’s house, both me and the chief baker:

tcz: Nikhat chu changlhah hompa le keiman mang chom cheh kanei lhon in ka mang lhon jong chu thusim chom cheh kanei lhon in,
en_web: We dreamed a dream in one night, he and I. Each man dreamed according to the interpretation of his dream.
en_kjv: and we dreamed a dream in one night, I and he; we dreamed each man according to the interpretation of his dream.

tcz: Hiche laiphat chun Hebrew khangthah khat lengpa songkul'a chun keiho toh ana um'in, ama chu lengpa semang pachong pa soh a jong ana pang ahi, kamang nei lhon chu kasei lhon in ahile chu'in aman kamang lhon chu eile doh peh lhon e ati.
en_web: There was with us there a young man, a Hebrew, servant to the captain of the guard, and we told him, and he interpreted to us our dreams. He interpreted to each man according to his dream.
en_kjv: And there was there with us a young man, a Hebrew, servant to the captain of the guard; and we told him, and he interpreted to us our dreams; to each man according to his dream he did interpret.

tcz: Chule aman eiledoh peh lhon bang bang chun ahung guilhung cheh in ahi, keiman kana toh ngai ngai eikitohsah in an vaihompa akikhai lihtan ahi.”
en_web: As he interpreted to us, so it was. He restored me to my office, and he hanged him.”
en_kjv: And it came to pass, as he interpreted to us, so it was; me he restored unto mine office, and him he hanged.

tcz: Pharaoh in Joseph chu ahol in mi asol paijeng tan ama chu agan a gang in songkul'a kon in ahin puidoh jeng uvin, chuin avon ho akikhel in chule akhamul ho a kisuhtheng in, hichun ama Pharaoh toh kimuto din alut tai.
en_web: Then Pharaoh sent and called Joseph, and they brought him hastily out of the dungeon. He shaved himself, changed his clothing, and came in to Pharaoh.
en_kjv: Then Pharaoh sent and called Joseph, and they brought him hastily out of the dungeon: and he shaved himself, and changed his raiment, and came in unto Pharaoh.

tcz: Hichun Pharaoh in Joseph koma aseitai, “Keiman janlhah in mang ka neijin koima chan ale doh theipon ahin keiman ka jah chu ahile mang kiti hohi nang man hetthei na nanei chu kana jai.”
en_web: Pharaoh said to Joseph, “I have dreamed a dream, and there is no one who can interpret it. I have heard it said of you, that when you hear a dream you can interpret it.”
en_kjv: And Pharaoh said unto Joseph, I have dreamed a dream, and there is none that can interpret it: and I have heard say of thee, that thou canst understand a dream to interpret it.

tcz: Joseph in adonbut in, “Hiche ho chu keima adinga thil hahsa ahi ati. Amavang Pathen in hiche ipi tina ham chu nahetsah theiye,” ati.
en_web: Joseph answered Pharaoh, saying, “It isn’t in me. God will give Pharaoh an answer of peace.”
en_kjv: And Joseph answered Pharaoh, saying, It is not in me: God shall give Pharaoh an answer of peace.

tcz: Chuin Pharaoh mang chu Joseph koma aseitai, aman hitin aseiye, “Ka mang in Nile vadung panga kana ding in.
en_web: Pharaoh spoke to Joseph, “In my dream, behold, I stood on the brink of the river;
en_kjv: And Pharaoh said unto Joseph, In my dream, behold, I stood upon the bank of the river:

tcz: Hiche a che a chun bongchal sagi hoitah kivah thao cheh vadunga kon chun ahung doh in chule hilaiya hampa dong ho chu ane pantan ahi.
en_web: and behold, seven fat and sleek cattle came up out of the river. They fed in the marsh grass;
en_kjv: and behold, there came up out of the river seven kine, fatfleshed and well favoured; and they fed in a meadow:

tcz: Hinlah keiman chom khat jouvin bongchal adang sagi agong a gong ahoimo cheh ahung potdoh kit ka mun, keiman hitabang gancha gong aphe umlou Egypt gamsunga ka hinkhon kana mukha hih laiye.
en_web: and behold, seven other cattle came up after them, poor and very ugly and thin, such as I never saw in all the land of Egypt for ugliness.
en_kjv: and behold, seven other kine came up after them, poor and very ill favoured and leanfleshed, such as I never saw in all the land of Egypt for badness:

tcz: Hiche bong agong melse tah hochun bongchal sagi athao ho chu aval lhum tan ahi.
en_web: The thin and ugly cattle ate up the first seven fat cattle;
en_kjv: and the lean and the ill favoured kine did eat up the first seven fat kine:

tcz: Amahon aval lhum jou chun koiman ipi kabol ham tia ahethei jong aumpoi, amahon aval lhum jou uchun abepbep ahiuvin, hichun keima ka hung khang dohtai.
en_web: and when they had eaten them up, it couldn’t be known that they had eaten them, but they were still ugly, as at the beginning. So I awoke.
en_kjv: and when they had eaten them up, it could not be known that they had eaten them; but they were still ill favoured, as at the beginning. So I awoke.

tcz: Hichun keima ka imu lhu kit'in, chule keiman mang khat kaneibe kit'in, hichea kamang achun changvui sagi vetnom umtah phungkhat a ga ka mun ahi.
en_web: I saw in my dream, and behold, seven heads of grain came up on one stalk, full and good;
en_kjv: And I saw in my dream, and behold, seven ears came up in one stalk, full and good:

tcz: Chule chang vui sagi machu akiveigeosa akeoseh cheh, nisolam khohui mut geosa cheh, khat ho nunga chun ahungdoh doh uvin ahi.
en_web: and behold, seven heads of grain, withered, thin, and blasted with the east wind, sprung up after them.
en_kjv: and behold, seven ears, withered, thin, and blasted with the east wind, sprung up after them:

tcz: Chuin changvui ageosa ho chun changvui hoitah hochu avallhum kittan, hiche kamang hohi doithem ho koma kaseiyin, Hinlah ka mangho chu ipi kisei na ham koima chan eihil chen theipoi ati.
en_web: The thin heads of grain swallowed up the seven good heads of grain. I told it to the magicians, but there was no one who could explain it to me.”
en_kjv: and the thin ears devoured the seven good ears: and I told this unto the magicians; but there was none that could declare it to me.

tcz: Joseph in adonbut in, “Pharaoh mang teni hi thakhat ahi, Pathen in Pharaoh hi ipi abol ding ahin hetsah masah ahi bouve.
en_web: Joseph said to Pharaoh, “The dream of Pharaoh is one. What God is about to do he has declared to Pharaoh.
en_kjv: And Joseph said unto Pharaoh, The dream of Pharaoh is one: God hath shewed Pharaoh what he is about to do.

tcz: Bongchal sagi athao ahoi ho chule changvui sagi vetnom nom uma, aga hon avet sah nom chu ahile kum sagi sunga hi neh le chah neng ding avetsah ahi,” ati.
en_web: The seven good cattle are seven years; and the seven good heads of grain are seven years. The dream is one.
en_kjv: The seven good kine are seven years; and the seven good ears are seven years: the dream is one.

tcz: Chule bongchal sagi agong hole Changvui sagi ageosa aphunga goden solam huiyin asemgot den hon avetsah chu ahile kum sagi nasa tah a kel hunglha ding chu avetsah ahi.
en_web: The seven thin and ugly cattle that came up after them are seven years, and also the seven empty heads of grain blasted with the east wind; they will be seven years of famine.
en_kjv: And the seven thin and ill favoured kine that came up after them are seven years; and the seven empty ears blasted with the east wind shall be seven years of famine.

tcz: Hiche hohi keiman ka phondoh banga hung guilhung ding ahi, Ajeh chu Pathen in Pharaoh hi aphat ahung lhun masanga ipi abol dingho chu ahin hetsah ahiye ati.
en_web: That is the thing which I have spoken to Pharaoh. God has shown Pharaoh what he is about to do.
en_kjv: This is the thing which I have spoken unto Pharaoh: What God is about to do he sheweth unto Pharaoh.

tcz: Tua patna Egypt gamsung a hi kum sagi hatah a neh le chah hung neng ding ahi.
en_web: Behold, seven years of great plenty throughout all the land of Egypt are coming.
en_kjv: Behold, there come seven years of great plenty throughout all the land of Egypt:

tcz: Amavang hiche joule chun kum sagi ma kel nasatah in hung lhan tin, chuteng chule chun Egypt gamsung ima ma ana tha lhing chu kisumil gam'a, kel lhah chun agamsung abah gam jeng ding ahi tai.
en_web: Seven years of famine will arise after them, and all the plenty will be forgotten in the land of Egypt. The famine will consume the land,
en_kjv: and there shall arise after them seven years of famine; and all the plenty shall be forgotten in the land of Egypt; and the famine shall consume the land;

tcz: Hiche kel hung khoh hi gimnei lheh jeng ding kum tamtah neh le chah ana ninglhin na ho jouse chu koiman agel doh lou ding ahitai.
en_web: and the plenty will not be known in the land by reason of that famine which follows; for it will be very grievous.
en_kjv: and the plenty shall not be known in the land by reason of that famine following; for it shall be very grievous.

tcz: Pharaoh mang teni ahung ki hetsah na thupi pen tah chu ahile, Pathen in na ahin toh vahding ahiti gontup sa ahi tai, hung lhung vah tei ding ahi ati.
en_web: The dream was doubled to Pharaoh, because the thing is established by God, and God will shortly bring it to pass.
en_kjv: And for that the dream was doubled unto Pharaoh twice; it is because the thing is established by God, and God will shortly bring it to pass.

tcz: Hijeh a chu Pharaoh in chingthei tah pasal chule thil hethem tah koitabang aholdoh a Egypt gamsung pumpia mopothei ahol angai tai.
en_web: “Now therefore let Pharaoh look for a discreet and wise man, and set him over the land of Egypt.
en_kjv: Now therefore let Pharaoh look out a man discreet and wise, and set him over the land of Egypt.

tcz: Hichun Pharaoh in agam agam a lamkai avetup ding mi lhengdoh henlang hiche teng chule louga sohho kum sagi neh anen sung chun hop nga lah a hop khat koidoh uhenlang,
en_web: Let Pharaoh do this, and let him appoint overseers over the land, and take up the fifth part of the land of Egypt’s produce in the seven plenteous years.
en_kjv: Let Pharaoh do this, and let him appoint officers over the land, and take up the fifth part of the land of Egypt in the seven plenteous years.

tcz: Pharaoh thanei na noiya tua patna neh le chah hiche kum sunga hatah a anen pet ahin changpang ahin koi dimset un, phatechan koitup uhenlang chule angah jong umjing hen, kho nung chan geiya khopi sunga neh le chah umjing thei nadin ati.
en_web: Let them gather all the food of these good years that come, and store grain under the hand of Pharaoh for food in the cities, and let them keep it.
en_kjv: And let them gather all the food of those good years that come, and lay up corn under the hand of Pharaoh, and let them keep food in the cities.

tcz: Tua chang le mim ho jouse hi phatechan mun khat a gamsung pumpin koikhom uhen, chutile kum sagi sunga nasatah a kel ahung khoh teng Egypt gam sunga mipi jouse kihinso thei ding ahi.
en_web: The food will be to supply the land against the seven years of famine, which will be in the land of Egypt; so that the land will not perish through the famine.”
en_kjv: And that food shall be for store to the land against the seven years of famine, which shall be in the land of Egypt; that the land perish not through the famine.

tcz: Hiche lungthim tohgon hi Pharaoh ahin ama semang pachong hon jong pha asa cheh tauvin ahi.
en_web: The thing was good in the eyes of Pharaoh, and in the eyes of all his servants.
en_kjv: And the thing was good in the eyes of Pharaoh, and in the eyes of all his servants.

tcz: Hichun Pharaoh in amaho chu adongin, “Eihon hitobang pasal Pathen lhagao chenna hi imujou dingu hi nam,” ati.
en_web: Pharaoh said to his servants, “Can we find such a one as this, a man in whom is the Spirit of God?”
en_kjv: And Pharaoh said unto his servants, Can we find such a one as this is, a man in whom the spirit of God is?

tcz: Hiche pet chun Pharaoh in Joseph ahoulimpi in, “Ajeh chu Pathen in ema jouse nangma nahetsah tah jeh in nang tobang koimacha ahethem le aching aumta poi.
en_web: Pharaoh said to Joseph, “Because God has shown you all of this, there is no one so discreet and wise as you.
en_kjv: And Pharaoh said unto Joseph, Forasmuch as God hath shewed thee all this, there is none so discreet and wise as thou art:

tcz: Nangma keima leng touna anatou ding ahitai, kamiten nangma thupeh jouse ajui cheh dingu ahitai. chule thil khat bou ikikhet nading chu keima kalengvai pohna bou lenjo ding kahi ati.
en_web: You shall be over my house. All my people will be ruled according to your word. Only in the throne I will be greater than you.”
en_kjv: thou shalt be over my house, and according unto thy word shall all my people be ruled: only in the throne will I be greater than thou.

tcz: Pharaoh in Joseph jah ah aseitan, “Keiman nangma hi Egypt gam sunga thanei na le mopoh na kapeh doh nahi tai ati.”
en_web: Pharaoh said to Joseph, “Behold, I have set you over all the land of Egypt.”
en_kjv: And Pharaoh said unto Joseph, See, I have set thee over all the land of Egypt.

tcz: Hichun Pharaoh in akhut a sana khutjem chu ala doh in Joseph khut a abupeh tai, Aman vonkang hoitah aki vonsah in chule sana khi jong angong a aki osah tai.
en_web: Pharaoh took off his signet ring from his hand, and put it on Joseph’s hand, and arrayed him in robes of fine linen, and put a gold chain about his neck.
en_kjv: And Pharaoh took off his ring from his hand, and put it upon Joseph’s hand, and arrayed him in vestures of fine linen, and put a gold chain about his neck;

tcz: Hichun lengpan Joseph chu asakol chunga atousah in amasanga chun “Mihon dilsu vo tin asamuvin ahi.” Hiti hin aman Joseph chu Egypt gam pumpi semang in ana pansah tai.
en_web: He made him ride in the second chariot which he had. They cried before him, “Bow the knee!” He set him over all the land of Egypt.
en_kjv: and he made him to ride in the second chariot which he had; and they cried before him, Bow the knee: and he made him ruler over all the land of Egypt.

tcz: Chule Pharaoh in Joseph kom a hitin aseiye, “Nangma phatsah louva Egypt gamsunga koima chan akhut alapthei lou ding, keima amina bou Pharaoh kahi ding ahi,” ati.
en_web: Pharaoh said to Joseph, “I am Pharaoh. Without you, no man shall lift up his hand or his foot in all the land of Egypt.”
en_kjv: And Pharaoh said unto Joseph, I am Pharaoh, and without thee shall no man lift up his hand or foot in all the land of Egypt.

tcz: Hichun Pharaoh in Joseph chu Egypt te min thah apen Zaphenath-paneah Potiphera chanu Asenath chu Joseph ji din Pharaoh in agontup peh in ahi, hiche apatna chu Joseph in Egypt gamsung a mopoh na alah ahitai.
en_web: Pharaoh called Joseph’s name Zaphenath-Paneah. He gave him Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera priest of On as a wife. Joseph went out over the land of Egypt.
en_kjv: And Pharaoh called Joseph’s name Zaphnath-paaneah; and he gave him to wife Asenath the daughter of Poti-pherah priest of On. And Joseph went out over all the land of Egypt.

tcz: Egypt lengpa Pharaoh koma anatong dinga alut chun Joseph kum somthum alhing tai. Chuin Joseph chu Pharaoh angsunga konin apotdoh in Egypt gam leiset pumpi aga kholsoh keiyin ahi.
en_web: Joseph was thirty years old when he stood before Pharaoh king of Egypt. Joseph went out from the presence of Pharaoh, and went throughout all the land of Egypt.
en_kjv: And Joseph was thirty years old when he stood before Pharaoh king of Egypt. And Joseph went out from the presence of Pharaoh, and went throughout all the land of Egypt.

tcz: Ana kisei bang chun kum sagi sung chun neh le chah lousoh hatah in apungin ahi.
en_web: In the seven plenteous years the earth produced abundantly.
en_kjv: And in the seven plenteous years the earth brought forth by handfuls.

tcz: Hiche kum sagi sunga chun Joseph in chang le mim Egypt gamsunga kimu jouse chu mun khat a akoikhom soh kei in, chule khopi jousea akoina mun asem soh kei in ahi.
en_web: He gathered up all the food of the seven years which were in the land of Egypt, and laid up the food in the cities. He stored food in each city from the fields around that city.
en_kjv: And he gathered up all the food of the seven years, which were in the land of Egypt, and laid up the food in the cities: the food of the field, which was round about every city, laid he up in the same.

tcz: Hichun Joseph in chang le mim chu tamtah avum leo in akhol khom in, vadung panga neldi bang in atam valtah jeh chun hetlut jou jong ahita pon, achaina langa chun simsen lou ahitan sim jong asim tapouve,
en_web: Joseph laid up grain as the sand of the sea, very much, until he stopped counting, for it was without number.
en_kjv: And Joseph gathered corn as the sand of the sea, very much, until he left numbering; for it was without number.

tcz: Kellhah kum hung lhun masang chun On thempu pa Potiphera chanu Asenath chun Joseph dingin chapa ni ana hinpeh-in
en_web: To Joseph were born two sons before the year of famine came, whom Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera priest of On, bore to him.
en_kjv: And unto Joseph were born two sons before the years of famine came, which Asenath the daughter of Poti-pherah priest of On bare unto him.

tcz: Joseph in achapa atahjo pa min chu Manasseh asah in, aman aseiyin, “Hiche hi ka Pathen in kagenthei na jouse eisuh milsahtai, chule kapa insung jong abonchaovin kasumil sohtai tina ahi.” (Manasseh: genthei tintang jouse suhmil na, chule insung mite jong mil jouta tina ahi).
en_web: Joseph called the name of the firstborn Manasseh, “For”, he said, “God has made me forget all my toil, and all my father’s house.”
en_kjv: And Joseph called the name of the firstborn Manasseh: For God, said he, hath made me forget all my toil, and all my father’s house.

tcz: Joseph in achapa aneojo pa min chu Ephraim asah tai, “Aman hitin aseiye, “Ka Pathen ka hahsat na le kagenthei na jeh in lolhin na eipe tai,” ati.
en_web: The name of the second, he called Ephraim: “For God has made me fruitful in the land of my affliction.”
en_kjv: And the name of the second called he Ephraim: For God hath caused me to be fruitful in the land of my affliction.

tcz: Egypt gamsunga kum sagi sunga chang le mim mang ketkut a ga jouse chu ahung kichai gamtan ahi.
en_web: The seven years of plenty, that were in the land of Egypt, came to an end.
en_kjv: And the seven years of plenteousness, that was in the land of Egypt, were ended.

tcz: Hichun kum sagi kel lhah ahung kipantan, Joseph in anasei doh mabang in hiche a nasa tah a kel hah chun anaivel a gam ho jouse jong asuboi soh heltai, ama vang Egypt gamsunga chun neh le chah ahahsat na emacha aumpoi.
en_web: The seven years of famine began to come, just as Joseph had said. There was famine in all lands, but in all the land of Egypt there was bread.
en_kjv: And the seven years of dearth began to come, according as Joseph had said: and the dearth was in all lands; but in all the land of Egypt there was bread.

tcz: Egypt gamsunga kel ahung khoh lheh jeng tan, hichun mipi ho chu neh le chah ngaichat jeh in Pharaoh koma ahung un, hichun Pharaoh in Egypt mipi teho chu “Joseph koma asol in aman bol un atiho chu bol uvin,” ati.
en_web: When all the land of Egypt was famished, the people cried to Pharaoh for bread, and Pharaoh said to all the Egyptians, “Go to Joseph. What he says to you, do.”
en_kjv: And when all the land of Egypt was famished, the people cried to Pharaoh for bread: and Pharaoh said unto all the Egyptians, Go unto Joseph; what he saith to you, do.

tcz: Hiti chun kel lhah chu hatah in ahung khohse cheh tan gamsung jouse aboilou aumta pon, Joseph in chang pang ho jouse chu ahong doh tan, Egypt mipite chu aki choh sah tai. Ajeh chu Egypt gamsunga kelkhoh chu asang lheh in hitobang kel hah chu ana umkha hihlaiye.
en_web: The famine was over all the surface of the earth. Joseph opened all the store houses, and sold to the Egyptians. The famine was severe in the land of Egypt.
en_kjv: And the famine was over all the face of the earth: and Joseph opened all the storehouses, and sold unto the Egyptians; and the famine waxed sore in the land of Egypt.

tcz: Chule gam dang dang Egypt gam kimvel a jousen neh le chah akichoh thei nadiuvin Joseph heng ahinnai lut tauvin, Ajeh chu hitobang kel hah chu vannoi leiset chung jouse asuh boi cheh ahi.
en_web: All countries came into Egypt, to Joseph, to buy grain, because the famine was severe in all the earth.
en_kjv: And all countries came into Egypt to Joseph for to buy corn; because that the famine was so sore in all lands.

tcz: Hichun Egypt ma anneh anendan chu Jacob in ahe tan, achate jah a asei tai, “Ibola na din chet chut uva kiveto nahiu ham?
en_web: Now Jacob saw that there was grain in Egypt, and Jacob said to his sons, “Why do you look at one another?”
en_kjv: Now when Jacob saw that there was corn in Egypt, Jacob said unto his sons, Why do ye look one upon another?

tcz: Keiman thusoh kajan Egypt gam lama chang aum e, hijeh chun nangho cheuvin lang neh ding gacho tauvin, eima ho ikihinso thei nadingu vin,” ati.
en_web: He said, “Behold, I have heard that there is grain in Egypt. Go down there, and buy for us from there, so that we may live, and not die.”
en_kjv: And he said, Behold, I have heard that there is corn in Egypt: get you down thither, and buy for us from thence; that we may live, and not die.

tcz: Hichun Joseph sopite ho mi som neh cho ding in Egypt lama asuh chetauvin ahi.
en_web: Joseph’s ten brothers went down to buy grain from Egypt.
en_kjv: And Joseph’s ten brethren went down to buy corn in Egypt.

tcz: Hinlah Jacob in vang Joseph sopipa Benjamin chu amaho lah a asol tapoi, aman aseiyin, “Keima katiya lheh tai ajole kisuh khah na le boina toh khante,” ati.
en_web: But Jacob didn’t send Benjamin, Joseph’s brother, with his brothers; for he said, “Lest perhaps harm happen to him.”
en_kjv: But Benjamin, Joseph’s brother, Jacob sent not with his brethren; for he said, Lest peradventure mischief befall him.

tcz: Canaan gam kel hah aum tah jeh chun Israel (Jacob) chate chu Egypt lama anneh hol din mijouse toh ahung lhung khom tauve.
en_web: The sons of Israel came to buy among those who came, for the famine was in the land of Canaan.
en_kjv: And the sons of Israel came to buy corn among those that came: for the famine was in the land of Canaan.

tcz: Tua hi Joseph chu Egypt gam'a chu gam vaihom ahitan, chule chang john a dinga thanei na jouse Joseph kipe ahi tan, hiche pettah chun asopite ahung lhung tauvin, amaho ahung lhun lhun un, hikoma chun tol'a ama ho abohkhup un akunsoh tauve.
en_web: Joseph was the governor over the land. It was he who sold to all the people of the land. Joseph’s brothers came, and bowed themselves down to him with their faces to the earth.
en_kjv: And Joseph was the governor over the land, and he it was that sold to all the people of the land: and Joseph’s brethren came, and bowed down themselves before him with their faces to the earth.

tcz: Joseph'in asopite chu amuphat in abonchauvin ahe soh keiyin, ahi vang in amaho chu hetphah lou bol in, hutot tah-in ahouvin, chule ajah uva, “Hoiya kona hung na hiuvem ong?” atile amahon jong “Canaan gam'a kon kahiuvin, puhsui dinga hung kahiuve,” atiuvin ahi.
en_web: Joseph saw his brothers, and he recognized them, but acted like a stranger to them, and spoke roughly with them. He said to them, “Where did you come from?” They said, “From the land of Canaan, to buy food.”
en_kjv: And Joseph saw his brethren, and he knew them, but made himself strange unto them, and spake roughly unto them; and he said unto them, Whence come ye? And they said, From the land of Canaan to buy food.

tcz: Joseph in asopiho chu ahet vang'in amahon ahe doh jou pouve.
en_web: Joseph recognized his brothers, but they didn’t recognize him.
en_kjv: And Joseph knew his brethren, but they knew not him.

tcz: Hichun Joseph in kum tamtah masang a asopi ho mang ana mat ho chu ahin geldoh in asopi ho koma hitin aseiye, “Nangho hi mipha lou le migucha nahiuve, keima ho gam hi lah mangthei ham ahiloule akihongbit joupouve, tia neihung khol leu ahi,” ati.
en_web: Joseph remembered the dreams which he dreamed about them, and said to them, “You are spies! You have come to see the nakedness of the land.”
en_kjv: And Joseph remembered the dreams which he dreamed of them, and said unto them, Ye are spies; to see the nakedness of the land you are come.

tcz: Ahipoi ka Pakai tin ama hon a donbut uvin, “Nasoh teho hi puhsui anneh hol a choh ding joh ka hi bouve.
en_web: They said to him, “No, my lord, but your servants have come to buy food.
en_kjv: And they said unto him, Nay, my lord, but to buy food are thy servants come.

tcz: Keiho jouse hi pa khat a hung peng cheh kahi bouve, milung theng ka hiuve, nasoh hohi miphalou kahi pouve!”
en_web: We are all one man’s sons; we are honest men. Your servants are not spies.”
en_kjv: We are all one man’s sons; we are true men, thy servants are no spies.

tcz: Ahin Joseph in a sei kit leuvin, “Ahipoi nangho hi ka gam'u hi gam ong kivaipoh achavaiye tia nei hung khol leu ahi,” ati.
en_web: He said to them, “No, but you have come to see the nakedness of the land!”
en_kjv: And he said unto them, Nay, but to see the nakedness of the land you are come.

tcz: Hinlah ama hon a donbut uvin, “nasoh teho hi ucha pasal som le ni kahiuvin, pa khatna hung peng ka hiuvin, Canaan gam'a incheng tuchung hin aneopen pa hi ka paotoh ka hin dalha uvin, chule mi khatpa vang aum tapoi.”
en_web: They said, “We, your servants, are twelve brothers, the sons of one man in the land of Canaan; and behold, the youngest is today with our father, and one is no more.”
en_kjv: And they said, Thy servants are twelve brethren, the sons of one man in the land of Canaan; and behold, the youngest is this day with our father, and one is not.

tcz: Joseph in adonbut in, “Keiman kasei banga nang ho hi michom miphalou na hiuve,” ati.
en_web: Joseph said to them, “It is like I told you, saying, ‘You are spies!’
en_kjv: And Joseph said unto them, That is it that I spake unto you, saying, Ye are spies:

tcz: Hichea hi nangma ho kapatep ding na hiuve, Pharaoh hinlahi sea hiche mun hi nada lhah lou ding'u, chule nasopi pau a lhumpen pa na hinpui kah seuva ati.
en_web: By this you shall be tested. By the life of Pharaoh, you shall not go out from here, unless your youngest brother comes here.
en_kjv: hereby ye shall be proved: By the life of Pharaoh ye shall not go forth hence, except your youngest brother come hither.

tcz: Nangho lah a mikhat kisol uvin lang amapa chun na sopi pau chu hinpui henlang, chule adangho se hilaiya na um ding'u, na thusei'u hi dihnam tia ka khol chil ding ahi; amavang hichu ahi loule Pharaoh ahin laisea nang ho hi michom, miphalou kiti chu na hiuve.
en_web: Send one of you, and let him get your brother, and you shall be bound, that your words may be tested, whether there is truth in you, or else by the life of Pharaoh surely you are spies.”
en_kjv: Send one of you, and let him fetch your brother, and ye shall be kept in prison, that your words may be proved, whether there be any truth in you: or else by the life of Pharaoh surely ye are spies.

tcz: Hichun Joseph in amaho chu abonchauvin songkul'a nithum jen ahen in ahi.
en_web: He put them all together into custody for three days.
en_kjv: And he put them all together into ward three days.

tcz: Nithum lhin nin Joseph in aseiyin, “Hiche hi bol uvin nahin thei nading uvin, ajeh chu keiman Pathen ka ging lheh jeng'e ati.
en_web: Joseph said to them the third day, “Do this, and live, for I fear God.
en_kjv: And Joseph said unto them the third day, This do, and live; for I fear God:

tcz: Nangho hi milung theng na hiu leh nangho lah a mikhat hi songkul'a umden uvin lang, ahin adangse se vang ki nungle cheh uvin, na insung mite din chang le mim kipoh un che tauvin ati.
en_web: If you are honest men, then let one of your brothers be bound in your prison; but you go, carry grain for the famine of your houses.
en_kjv: if ye be true men, let one of your brethren be bound in the house of your prison: go ye, carry corn for the famine of your houses:

tcz: Chule na sopi pau alhumpen pachu keima koma nahin pui dingu, na thusei houchu dihnam tia kakhol chil ding ahi. Chule nangho nathi lou dingu,” hiti chun amahon jong akisei chu abol'un ahiye.
en_web: Bring your youngest brother to me; so will your words be verified, and you won’t die.” They did so.
en_kjv: but bring your youngest brother unto me; so shall your words be verified, and ye shall not die. And they did so.

tcz: Hichun amaho khat le khat akihou lim un, “Adih tah a sei dinga eiho hi isopi pau Joseph ibolset jeh uva gotna ichan'u ahi tai atiuve. Ajeh chu eihon imusoh kei jun aman ahinkho huhdoh na ding in a taovin, hinlah eihon inahsah pouve, hiche ho jeh a chu tua hi gotna ho hi eiho chunga hung chu ahitai atiuve.
en_web: They said to one another, “We are certainly guilty concerning our brother, in that we saw the distress of his soul, when he begged us, and we wouldn’t listen. Therefore this distress has come upon us.”
en_kjv: And they said one to another, We are verily guilty concerning our brother, in that we saw the anguish of his soul, when he besought us, and we would not hear; therefore is this distress come upon us.

tcz: Hichun Reuben in amaho chu hitin adonbut in, “Keiman kasei hilou ham, chapang chu imachan bolse hih un, ahin ka thusei nangai pouvin, tua eihon ama thisan man chu isah diu ahitai.”
en_web: Reuben answered them, saying, “Didn’t I tell you, saying, ‘Don’t sin against the child,’ and you wouldn’t listen? Therefore also, behold, his blood is required.”
en_kjv: And Reuben answered them, saying, Spake I not unto you, saying, Do not sin against the child; and ye would not hear? therefore, behold, also his blood is required.

tcz: Ahin amahon Joseph thusei chu ahe doh pouve, ajeh chu amaho ki kah lah a paole apan jeh jal ahi.
en_web: They didn’t know that Joseph understood them; for there was an interpreter between them.
en_kjv: And they knew not that Joseph understood them; for he spake unto them by an interpreter.

tcz: Hinlah Joseph a kihei doh in achom lang angan akap tai, ahin ama ahung kinung hei kitin avel in amaho jah thei dingin ahoulim in, hichun amaho lah a Simeon chu alheng doh in amaho mitmu tah in akan tup tai.
en_web: He turned himself away from them, and wept. Then he returned to them, and spoke to them, and took Simeon from among them, and bound him before their eyes.
en_kjv: And he turned himself about from them, and wept; and returned to them again, and communed with them, and took from them Simeon, and bound him before their eyes.

tcz: Hichun Joseph in thu apen, amaho dipsunga chun chang khum peh uvin, chule sum ho jong chu ama ama dipsunga nung hetpeh un, chule lampia aneh dingu jong gonpeh uvin hiti chun amaho din thil gontup in aumtai.
en_web: Then Joseph gave a command to fill their bags with grain, and to restore each man’s money into his sack, and to give them food for the way. So it was done to them.
en_kjv: Then Joseph commanded to fill their sacks with corn, and to restore every man’s money into his sack, and to give them provision for the way: and thus did he unto them.

tcz: Hichun asopi hon sangan chung a chun nehding chang chu ahengdoh un a inlamu ahin jon tauve.
en_web: They loaded their donkeys with their grain, and departed from there.
en_kjv: And they laded their asses with the corn, and departed thence.

tcz: Ahin jan na akingah naova amaho lah a mikhat pa chun sangan an neh peh ding agotan adipsung chu agah hon doh le adip sunga sum dangka chu ahin mudoh tan ahi.
en_web: As one of them opened his sack to give his donkey food in the lodging place, he saw his money. Behold, it was in the mouth of his sack.
en_kjv: And as one of them opened his sack to give his ass provender in the inn, he espied his money; for behold, it was in his sack’s mouth.

tcz: Veuvin tin asopiho jah a aseiyin, “Kasum hohi ka dipsunga eiki nungkoi peh kit tai,” hichun amaho chu alungu alhadeh tauvin kithing pum pum in khat le khat akihou khom un, “Pathen in ipi eito sah u hi tante atiuve.”
en_web: He said to his brothers, “My money is restored! Behold, it is in my sack!” Their hearts failed them, and they turned trembling to one another, saying, “What is this that God has done to us?”
en_kjv: And he said unto his brethren, My money is restored; and lo, it is even in my sack: and their heart failed them, and they were afraid, saying one to another, What is this that God hath done unto us?

tcz: Hichun amahon apao Jacob heng Canaan gamsung ahung lhung kit tauvin, hichun ama hon Jacob koma thil ahinto hou chu aseipeh un, hitin aseiyui.
en_web: They came to Jacob their father, to the land of Canaan, and told him all that had happened to them, saying,
en_kjv: And they came unto Jacob their father unto the land of Canaan, and told him all that befell unto them; saying,

tcz: “Gamneipa chun hiti hin aw sangtah in keiho jah din asam in, chule keiho hi miphalou gamsunga thilse bol ding in eigingmo un ahi.
en_web: “The man, the lord of the land, spoke roughly with us, and took us for spies of the country.
en_kjv: The man, who is the lord of the land, spake roughly to us, and took us for spies of the country.

tcz: Hinlah keihon amapa chu ka donbut un, keiho hi milung theng miki tah ka hi bouve ka tiuvin, chule keiho miphaloute ka hipouve.
en_web: We said to him, ‘We are honest men. We are no spies.
en_kjv: And we said unto him, We are true men; we are no spies:

tcz: Chule keima hohi ucha sopi som le ni solam a hung kon ka hiuvin, Pakhat in eihin'u ahin, mikhat vang ahing tapon chule aneo pen pa vang tuhin ka pao toh Canaan gamsunga ka hin dalha uve.
en_web: We are twelve brothers, sons of our father; one is no more, and the youngest is today with our father in the land of Canaan.’
en_kjv: we be twelve brethren, sons of our father; one is not, and the youngest is this day with our father in the land of Canaan.

tcz: Hichun gamsung a lamkai pipu pa chun hitin eisei peh uve, nangma ho hi hitia ka bol ding mipha milung theng nahiu kahet doh nadin, nangho lah a khat ki dalhau vin, chule adanghon an neh ding chang le mim pouvin lang na inkote kom lang nung che tauvin.
en_web: The man, the lord of the land, said to us, ‘By this I will know that you are honest men: leave one of your brothers with me, and take grain for the famine of your houses, and go your way.
en_kjv: And the man, the lord of the country, said unto us, Hereby shall I know that ye are true men; leave one of your brethren here with me, and take food for the famine of your households, and be gone:

tcz: Hinlah na sopipau alhumpen pachu ka henga na hin puilut tei ding'u ahi ati, chule keiman hiche jou teng chule nang hohi mipha midih tah nahiu, michom le mikhol na hi pouve tichu kahet chet ding ahitai. Hiche teng chule nasopi pau chu kanung peh kit diu chule nanghon boina umlouva navah sel a an jong nakihol theiyu ahi,” ati.
en_web: Bring your youngest brother to me. Then I will know that you are not spies, but that you are honest men. So I will deliver your brother to you, and you shall trade in the land.’”
en_kjv: and bring your youngest brother unto me: then shall I know that ye are no spies, but that ye are true men: so will I deliver you your brother, and ye shall traffick in the land.

tcz: Adip'u chu alhei lha uvin ahile vetan amitakip in asum chun cheh chu ama ama dip sung cheh a ana umsoh keiyin; ama hon jong apaovin jong a sumchun chengseu chu amudoh phat uvin akihot lhul gam tauve.
en_web: As they emptied their sacks, behold, each man’s bundle of money was in his sack. When they and their father saw their bundles of money, they were afraid.
en_kjv: And it came to pass as they emptied their sacks, that behold, every man’s bundle of money was in his sack: and when both they and their father saw the bundles of money, they were afraid.

tcz: Jacob chu tijatah'in ahoulim in, “Nangho hin ka chate ho neiguh mang peh cheh dingu ahi tai, Joseph jong aum ta pon, Simeon jong aum ta pon, chule tua nang hon Benjamin jong nei puimang peh kigo kit'un, na thil bol jouseu hi keima douna jeng ahi tai!”
en_web: Jacob, their father, said to them, “You have bereaved me of my children! Joseph is no more, Simeon is no more, and you want to take Benjamin away. All these things are against me.”
en_kjv: And Jacob their father said unto them, Me have ye bereaved of my children: Joseph is not, and Simeon is not, and ye will take Benjamin away: all these things are against me.

tcz: Hichun Reuben in apa Jacob chu a donbut in, “Benjamin chu ka hin nungpui louleh ka chate ni hi na deidei nalo thei ahitai, chule keiman Benjamin na ding in mopo nang kate ati, chule thonlouva kahin nungpui kit teitei ding ahi,” ati.
en_web: Reuben spoke to his father, saying, “Kill my two sons, if I don’t bring him to you. Entrust him to my care, and I will bring him to you again.”
en_kjv: And Reuben spake unto his father, saying, Slay my two sons, if I bring him not to thee: deliver him into my hand, and I will bring him to thee again.

tcz: Ahin Jacob in a donbut in, “Ka chapa chu nangma toh chelou ding ahi, ajeh chu aupa Joseph jong athi tan, tua kanei ka lungmonpi ama bou ahi tai; ijem tin lamkim lang nagei tengu le lamkah lah a toset tohkha ta hen lang hile kasam kan nung jenga jong lunghema thikhol khul a neilhoh lut pai tah bah dingu ahibouve,” ati.
en_web: He said, “My son shall not go down with you; for his brother is dead, and he only is left. If harm happens to him along the way in which you go, then you will bring down my gray hairs with sorrow to Sheol.”
en_kjv: And he said, My son shall not go down with you; for his brother is dead, and he is left alone: if mischief befall him by the way in the which ye go, then shall ye bring down my gray hairs with sorrow to the grave.

tcz: Tuhin Canaan gamsunga kel lhah chu akhoh cheh cheh jeng in ahi.
en_web: The famine was severe in the land.
en_kjv: And the famine was sore in the land.

tcz: Egypt gam'a kon a ahinpoh'u anchang aneh chai phat un hichun apao Jacob in achate jah a aseitai, “Nung che kit unlang neh ding gacho kit tauvin,” ati.
en_web: When they had eaten up the grain which they had brought out of Egypt, their father said to them, “Go again, buy us a little more food.”
en_kjv: And it came to pass, when they had eaten up the corn which they had brought out of Egypt, their father said unto them, Go again, buy us a little food.

tcz: Ahin Judah in apa Jacob a donbut in, “Gamsung lamkai pa chun hatah in eigah un, na sopi pao chu nahin puilou ule kamai namu lou dingu ahi,” ati.
en_web: Judah spoke to him, saying, “The man solemnly warned us, saying, ‘You shall not see my face, unless your brother is with you.’
en_kjv: And Judah spake unto him, saying, The man did solemnly protest unto us, saying, Ye shall not see my face, except your brother be with you.

tcz: Benjamin keiho toh na sol khom le kache dingu anchang kaga choh dingu ahi ati.
en_web: If you’ll send our brother with us, we’ll go down and buy you food;
en_kjv: If thou wilt send our brother with us, we will go down and buy thee food:

tcz: Amavang Benjamin che ding naphal loule keiho jong kache lou hel ding'u ahi taiti geldoh in, ajeh chu gamsung lamkai pa chun aseiye, “Na sopi pao alhum pen pachu nahin pui lou ule kamai namu lou dingu ahi atisa ahi.”
en_web: but if you don’t send him, we won’t go down, for the man said to us, ‘You shall not see my face, unless your brother is with you.’”
en_kjv: but if thou wilt not send him, we will not go down: for the man said unto us, Ye shall not see my face, except your brother be with you.

tcz: Hichun Jacob in adonbut in, “Ibol a nang hon nei suh genthei ju hitam, hiche gamvai popa koma chu sopi khat ka nei nalai uve tia nahin seidoh uham,” ati.
en_web: Israel said, “Why did you treat me so badly, telling the man that you had another brother?”
en_kjv: And Israel said, Wherefore dealt ye so ill with me, as to tell the man whether ye had yet a brother?

tcz: Amahon a donbut un, “Hiche gamsung lamkai pa chun eiho insung chan chin thu hoitah in aman thudoh eineijun, napao dam nalai em tin eidong un, hiche a chun keihon amapa thudoh ho chu ka donbut cheh un, chule keima hon iti ka het thei diu ham? na sopi pao hinpui yun ati ding chu,” atiuve.
en_web: They said, “The man asked directly concerning ourselves, and concerning our relatives, saying, ‘Is your father still alive? Have you another brother?’ We just answered his questions. Is there any way we could know that he would say, ‘Bring your brother down’?”
en_kjv: And they said, The man asked us straitly of our state, and of our kindred, saying, Is your father yet alive? have ye another brother? and we told him according to the tenor of these words: could we certainly know that he would say, Bring your brother down?

tcz: Judah in apa Israel koma asei tan, “Chapang pachu hin sol in hiche teng chule keiho kaga che diu ahi, chule eiho jouse le echateu jouse iki hinso thei ding'u ahi ati.
en_web: Judah said to Israel, his father, “Send the boy with me, and we’ll get up and go, so that we may live, and not die, both we, and you, and also our little ones.
en_kjv: And Judah said unto Israel his father, Send the lad with me, and we will arise and go; that we may live, and not die, both we, and thou, and also our little ones.

tcz: Chule keima ka tahsa tah in mopo nang kate ijem tia boina aum khah le, ahin Benjamin chu kahin nung pui loule boina jouse keiman mo ka poh ding ahi ati; chule nangma angsunga mopoh na thepmo na jouse keima chunga chu jeng hen ati.
en_web: I’ll be collateral for him. From my hand will you require him. If I don’t bring him to you, and set him before you, then let me bear the blame forever;
en_kjv: I will be surety for him; of my hand shalt thou require him: if I bring him not unto thee, and set him before thee, then let me bear the blame for ever:

tcz: Amavang eiho ana geisang hih leu hen tuphat a hi nivei tobang kilhung thei ding ahitai.”
en_web: for if we hadn’t delayed, surely we would have returned a second time by now.”
en_kjv: for except we had lingered, surely now we had returned this second time.

tcz: Chuphat in apao Israel chun ajah uva, ‘chuti ding mong ahiya ahile hiti hin ki gong uvin, gamsunga thingga phalai cheh lheng khom uvin lang, thingnai, lou them khat le khoiju them khat toh, thil namtwi toh, thei chang toh, chule jonmot chang toh nadip sunguva mipa peh ding chun posuh uvin ati.’
en_web: Their father, Israel, said to them, “If it must be so, then do this: Take from the choice fruits of the land in your bags, and carry down a present for the man, a little balm, a little honey, spices and myrrh, nuts, and almonds;
en_kjv: And their father Israel said unto them, If it must be so now, do this; take of the best fruits in the land in your vessels, and carry down the man a present, a little balm, and a little honey, spices, and myrrh, nuts, and almonds:

tcz: Chule dangka jong athop in pohbe un, ajeh chu na dip sung uva anaki koi chu koitobang khat in jong anabol khel jong himai thei ahi.
en_web: and take double money in your hand, and take back the money that was returned in the mouth of your sacks. Perhaps it was an oversight.
en_kjv: and take double money in your hand; and the money that was brought again in the mouth of your sacks, carry it again in your hand; peradventure it was an oversight:

tcz: Hijeh chun nasopi pao hi pui jun lang gamsung lamkai heng a nung che tauvin.
en_web: Take your brother also, get up, and return to the man.
en_kjv: take also your brother, and arise, go again unto the man:

tcz: Chule hatchung nung Pathen in phatthei naboh maiju hen, hiche gamsung vaipo mit mua jong ngailut na mel na chan thei na diuvin ati, chule nangma hon na sopi pao Simeon chule Benjamin na hin hen ohna lou dingu vin, chule keima vang ka chate jal'a thilo pai ding ka hitai,” ati.
en_web: May God Almighty give you mercy before the man, that he may release to you your other brother and Benjamin. If I am bereaved of my children, I am bereaved.”
en_kjv: and God Almighty give you mercy before the man, that he may send away your other brother, and Benjamin. If I be bereaved of my children, I am bereaved.

tcz: Hichun amahon Jacob thilpeh ho chu agongtup un, chule adipsung uva sum jong athop in apoh be uvin, Benjamin toh akilhon tauve; hichun amaho Egypt gam alhung taovin Joseph masanga a ding tauvin ahi.
en_web: The men took that present, and they took double money in their hand, and Benjamin; and got up, went down to Egypt, and stood before Joseph.
en_kjv: And the men took that present, and they took double money in their hand, and Benjamin; and rose up, and went down to Egypt, and stood before Joseph.

tcz: Chuin Joseph in Benjamin amaho lah a ahung chu amutan, hichun aman a insunga lhacha a pangho jah a hitin aseiye, “Amaho toh'in tunia an nekho ding ka hiuvin hijeh chun insung lama ana puilut un, chule gancha ana that un, kin thupitah kimang ding ahi.”
en_web: When Joseph saw Benjamin with them, he said to the steward of his house, “Bring the men into the house, and butcher an animal, and prepare; for the men will dine with me at noon.”
en_kjv: And when Joseph saw Benjamin with them, he said to the ruler of his house, Bring these men home, and slay, and make ready; for these men shall dine with me at noon.

tcz: Hichun lhacha hon Joseph in asei bang chun abol'un, amaho sese chu Joseph inlam a apuitau vin ahi.
en_web: The man did as Joseph commanded, and the man brought the men to Joseph’s house.
en_kjv: And the man did as Joseph bade; and the man brought the men into Joseph’s house.

tcz: Joseph insung a akipui lut jengu amudoh phat’ uvin miho chu aki chau vin, “Iche masah uva idip sunguva sum anaki nung hetlut jeh a hikoma hi eipui lut'uva, chutia chu mi khat hin hehset neu neuva, kitaole na einei dingu chuteng le eiho chengse soh a einei uva chule isangan teu aboncha akilah got hiya ahitai,” akiti uve.
en_web: The men were afraid, because they were brought to Joseph’s house; and they said, “Because of the money that was returned in our sacks the first time, we’re brought in; that he may seek occasion against us, attack us, and seize us as slaves, along with our donkeys.”
en_kjv: And the men were afraid, because they were brought into Joseph’s house; and they said, Because of the money that was returned in our sacks at the first time are we brought in; that he may seek occasion against us, and fall upon us, and take us for bondmen, and our asses.

tcz: Judah le asopihon Joseph insunga lhacha lamkai pa koma ache un akelkot koma hitin asei uve.
en_web: They came near to the steward of Joseph’s house, and they spoke to him at the door of the house,
en_kjv: And they came near to the steward of Joseph’s house, and they communed with him at the door of the house,

tcz: Amaho atao vun; Ja umtah pu, keima ho hi phat masa chun Egypt gam'a anchang cho a ka hung uve.
en_web: and said, “Oh, my lord, we indeed came down the first time to buy food.
en_kjv: and said, O sir, we came indeed down at the first time to buy food:

tcz: Ahin keiho kaki nungle uchun jan ahiphat in ka dip sungu kahon doh ule hichun keihon ka dipsung uva dangka thil choh na man ho chu mijouse dipsunga ana umsoh keiye, tuhin hiche dangka ho chu ka hin nungpoh cheh nauve.
en_web: When we came to the lodging place, we opened our sacks, and behold, each man’s money was in the mouth of his sack, our money in full weight. We have brought it back in our hand.
en_kjv: and it came to pass, when we came to the inn, that we opened our sacks, and behold, every man’s money was in the mouth of his sack, our money in full weight: and we have brought it again in our hand.

tcz: Chule keihon chang chohbe nading dangka jong ka hin pohbe uvin, koi tobang ham khat in dangka ho ka dipsung uva ana koi jong chu ka pum het pouve.
en_web: We have brought down other money in our hand to buy food. We don’t know who put our money in our sacks.”
en_kjv: And other money have we brought down in our hands to buy food: we cannot tell who put our money in our sacks.

tcz: Imacha lungboina nei hih un, tin insung lhacha pa chun aseiye, Na Pakai na pate Pathen chun na dipsung uva nahin koipeh'u ahi, na dangka hou jong keima koma aum nai; hichun aman Simeon chu alha kang in amaho laha ahinpui dohtan ahi.
en_web: He said, “Peace be to you. Don’t be afraid. Your God, and the God of your father, has given you treasure in your sacks. I received your money.” He brought Simeon out to them.
en_kjv: And he said, Peace be to you, fear not: your God, and the God of your father, hath given you treasure in your sacks: I had your money. And he brought Simeon out unto them.

tcz: Insung lhacha pa chun miho chu Joseph leng insung lama apuilut tauvin ahi, insung lhacha pan twi akengu kisil ngim na ding apen chule sangan ho ding anneh jong ape uvin ahi.
en_web: The man brought the men into Joseph’s house, and gave them water, and they washed their feet. He gave their donkeys fodder.
en_kjv: And the man brought the men into Joseph’s house, and gave them water, and they washed their feet; and he gave their asses provender.

tcz: Hichun amahon Joseph peh dinga ahin thilpoh houchu akigon tup uvin, chule amahon aja tauvin sunteng le Joseph toh an aneh khom ding'u thu chu;
en_web: They prepared the present for Joseph’s coming at noon, for they heard that they should eat bread there.
en_kjv: And they made ready the present against Joseph came at noon: for they heard that they should eat bread there.

tcz: Hichun Joseph in ahung lhun chun amahon athil poh'u chu ahin la doh un Joseph masanga tol'a abohkhup tauvin ahi.
en_web: When Joseph came home, they brought him the present which was in their hand into the house, and bowed themselves down to the earth before him.
en_kjv: And when Joseph came home, they brought him the present which was in their hand into the house, and bowed themselves to him to the earth.

tcz: Amahon alemjou chun adong tan napao akum atam tai nati pao chu “Dam jinga hinam, ama chu dam dam a hinam tin adong in ahi.”
en_web: He asked them of their welfare, and said, “Is your father well, the old man of whom you spoke? Is he yet alive?”
en_kjv: And he asked them of their welfare, and said, Is your father well, the old man of whom ye spake? Is he yet alive?

tcz: Amahon adon but un, “Henge adam dam nai atiuve,” chule nasohte keiho dinga ka pao chu adam in ahing na laiye,” chuin amaho Joseph ma sanga abohkhup kit uvin ahi.
en_web: They said, “Your servant, our father, is well. He is still alive.” They bowed down humbly.
en_kjv: And they answered, Thy servant our father is in good health, he is yet alive. And they bowed down their heads, and made obeisance.

tcz: Hichun Joseph in asopipa Benjamin chu aven “Amahi ham na sopiu alhum pen pa na tiu chu tin Joseph in adong tai,” Pathen in na umpi jingta hen O ka chapa!” ati.
en_web: He lifted up his eyes, and saw Benjamin, his brother, his mother’s son, and said, “Is this your youngest brother, of whom you spoke to me?” He said, “God be gracious to you, my son.”
en_kjv: And he lift up his eyes, and saw his brother Benjamin, his mother’s son, and said, Is this your younger brother, of whom ye spake unto me? And he said, God be gracious unto thee, my son.

tcz: Hichun Joseph ama umna insung dena kon in apot doh in, ajeh chu asopipa amu chun ama akitim joutapon, hichun ama indan sungnunga alutin agakaptan ahi.
en_web: Joseph hurried, for his heart yearned over his brother; and he sought a place to weep. He entered into his room, and wept there.
en_kjv: And Joseph made haste; for his bowels did yern upon his brother: and he sought where to weep; and he entered into his chamber, and wept there.

tcz: Chuin amai akiphet jouvin ama ahung potdoh kit in nasatah in akitim ham ham in, “An neh ding hin thuh taovin,” ati.
en_web: He washed his face, and came out. He controlled himself, and said, “Serve the meal.”
en_kjv: And he washed his face, and went out, and refrained himself, and said, Set on bread.

tcz: Hijeh chun amahon Joseph ding atum in, amaho ding atumin, chule ama toh nekhom ding Egypt mite ding atumin ankong asem tauve, ijeh inem itile Egypt miten Hebrew mite toh an aneh khom ngailouvu, neh khom ding chu Egypt mite dinga bohna khat hiya ahiye.
en_web: They served him by himself, and them by themselves, and the Egyptians who ate with him by themselves, because the Egyptians don’t eat with the Hebrews, for that is an abomination to the Egyptians.
en_kjv: And they set on for him by himself, and for them by themselves, and for the Egyptians, which did eat with him, by themselves: because the Egyptians might not eat bread with the Hebrews, for that is an abomination unto the Egyptians.

tcz: Joseph in asopiho chu atouna din akoi peh cheh in, ama hon jong ajalheh jeng un, amaho tahsa kum alen penna pat aneopen pa gei in atou nao agontup peh in atou sah tan ahi.
en_web: They sat before him, the firstborn according to his birthright, and the youngest according to his youth, and the men marveled with one another.
en_kjv: And they sat before him, the firstborn according to his birthright, and the youngest according to his youth: and the men marvelled one at another.

tcz: Amoho chan ding chu Joseph chan lah akon in asoh doh uvin ahi; chujong le Benjamin chan chu amaho khat chan jat sangin chan ajat ngan atam joi. Hitobang chun ama hon Joseph chutoh an ane khom uvin adon khom tauvin ahi.
en_web: He sent portions to them from before him, but Benjamin’s portion was five times as much as any of theirs. They drank, and were merry with him.
en_kjv: And he took and sent messes unto them from before him: but Benjamin’s mess was five times so much as any of theirs. And they drunk, and were merry with him.

tcz: Hichun asopiho chu cheding in aki gong tauvin, Joseph in insung lhacha ho lah a aseitan, “Amaho dipsunga chun apoh thei jat u dimset in anchang kipoh sah un, chule dangka ahin kipoh hou chu nunghet peh cheh kitun,” ati.
en_web: He commanded the steward of his house, saying, “Fill the men’s sacks with food, as much as they can carry, and put each man’s money in his sack’s mouth.
en_kjv: And he commanded the steward of his house, saying, Fill the men’s sacks with food, as much as they can carry, and put every man’s money in his sack’s mouth.

tcz: Chuteng le keima sum eng cha khon chu alhumpen pa dipsunga achung tho pena koi jun chule chang choh na dinga sum ahin kipoh toh chun koi than, hiti chun insung lhacha pan jong Joseph in asei bang chun aboltan ahi.
en_web: Put my cup, the silver cup, in the sack’s mouth of the youngest, with his grain money.” He did according to the word that Joseph had spoken.
en_kjv: And put my cup, the silver cup, in the sack’s mouth of the youngest, and his corn money. And he did according to the word that Joseph had spoken.

tcz: Jingkah matah in akipat doh un ache tauve, a sangan ho jong vumlet set in neh ding apon alampiu majon ding in asol tauve.
en_web: As soon as the morning was light, the men were sent away, they and their donkeys.
en_kjv: As soon as the morning was light, the men were sent away, they and their asses.

tcz: Amaho chu khopia kon chun achedoh nauvin gamla pi agei masang uvin Joseph in jong ainsung thil chingpa jah a chun, “kipat doh in lang miho nung chu del loiyin, amaho chu naphah teng le ajah uva, “Ipi ding pen tah a ka phat nau thilpha chu git louva na lethuh u-hitam ong? Ipi dinga keima dangka khon chu nana guh mangu ham?
en_web: When they had gone out of the city, and were not yet far off, Joseph said to his steward, “Up, follow after the men. When you overtake them, ask them, ‘Why have you rewarded evil for good?
en_kjv: And when they were gone out of the city, and not yet far off, Joseph said unto his steward, Up, follow after the men; and when thou dost overtake them, say unto them, Wherefore have ye rewarded evil for good?

tcz: Nangho hin ibola kapupa sum eng cha khon na guh'u hitam? Aman hiche chu aman chah a thil ahung lhung ding ho hetna a aneiji ahi; nanghon thilpha loutah na boldoh'u hi talou ham ati.
en_web: Isn’t this that from which my lord drinks, and by which he indeed divines? You have done evil in so doing.’”
en_kjv: Is not this it in which my lord drinketh, and whereby indeed he divineth? ye have done evil in so doing.

tcz: Insung lhacha pan amaho chu amat tup jouvin hitin aseitai.
en_web: He overtook them, and he spoke these words to them.
en_kjv: And he overtook them, and he spake unto them these same words.

tcz: Amahon amapa koma hi tin aseiuve, “Keima ho hi na soh ka hiuvin, chule keima hon hitobang chu ka bol lou beh ding'u ahi,” ati.
en_web: They said to him, “Why does my lord speak such words as these? Far be it from your servants that they should do such a thing!
en_kjv: And they said unto him, Wherefore saith my lord these words? God forbid that thy servants should do according to this thing:

tcz: Ven keiho Canaan gam'a patna sum dangka chu kahin ki choi cheh nauve, chule kadip sung uva ana umho chu ka Pakai pa in na kona kei hon iti dana sum eng chakhon chu ka guh doh thei diu ham atiuve.
en_web: Behold, the money, which we found in our sacks’ mouths, we brought again to you out of the land of Canaan. How then should we steal silver or gold out of your lord’s house?
en_kjv: behold, the money, which we found in our sacks’ mouths, we brought again unto thee out of the land of Canaan: how then should we steal out of thy lord’s house silver or gold?

tcz: Nasohte lah a koi hijongle ala ana umtah le ama jong chu thidoh maita hen, chule keiho jong ka pakai pa koma soh chang ding kahi tauve.
en_web: With whomever of your servants it is found, let him die, and we also will be my lord’s slaves.”
en_kjv: With whomsoever of thy servants it be found, both let him die, and we also will be my lord’s bondmen.

tcz: Hiche chu apha lheh jenge tin ama pan adonbut e, “Hinlah ka chakhon gupa bou chu ka soh a pang ding ahi ati tai, adangho vang imacha kalo louding adangho che tauvin,” ati.
en_web: He said, “Now also let it be according to your words. He with whom it is found will be my slave; and you will be blameless.”
en_kjv: And he said, Now also let it be according unto your words: he with whom it is found shall be my servant; and ye shall be blameless.

tcz: Amahon gangtah in adip hou chu sangan chunga kon in adom lha uvin ahong doh un ahi.
en_web: Then they hurried, and each man took his sack down to the ground, and each man opened his sack.
en_kjv: Then they speedily took down every man his sack to the ground, and opened every man his sack.

tcz: Hiphat chun insung lhacha pan alenpen apat in aneo pen pa gei in adip sung ahin kholtan ahile sum eng chakhon chu Benjamin dipsunga ahin mudoh tan ahi.
en_web: He searched, beginning with the oldest, and ending at the youngest. The cup was found in Benjamin’s sack.
en_kjv: And he searched, and began at the eldest, and left at the youngest: and the cup was found in Benjamin’s sack.

tcz: Hichun ama hon a sangkhol'u abot tel tel tauvin, apot hou chu a sangan chunga aheng doh kit un, khopi lam ahin nung jot kit tauve.
en_web: Then they tore their clothes, and each man loaded his donkey, and returned to the city.
en_kjv: Then they rent their clothes, and laded every man his ass, and returned to the city.

tcz: Judah le asopi ho ahung lhun u chun Joseph chu a in na ana umna laiye, chule amaho Joseph masanga tol ah abohkhup tauvin ahi.
en_web: Judah and his brothers came to Joseph’s house, and he was still there. They fell on the ground before him.
en_kjv: And Judah and his brethren came to Joseph’s house; for he was yet there: and they fell before him on the ground.

tcz: Chuin Joseph in amaho jah a aseiyin, “Ipi ham nanghon na bol'u hi? Nang hon na het lou'u ham hitobang mihem ho hi keiman amaho khonung ding kasei thei ahi,” ati.
en_web: Joseph said to them, “What deed is this that you have done? Don’t you know that such a man as I can indeed do divination?”
en_kjv: And Joseph said unto them, What deed is this that ye have done? wot ye not that such a man as I can certainly divine?

tcz: Hichun Judah in asei tai, “Ipi ka sei dingu hitam? keima ho iti them ka kichan diu hitam Pathen in nasohte chonsetna hohi ahin het dohsah ahi tai. Hijeh chun keiho ka boncha uva sum eng chakhon kimat doh na pa toh ka pakai pa soh a pang ding ka hitauve.
en_web: Judah said, “What will we tell my lord? What will we speak? How will we clear ourselves? God has found out the iniquity of your servants. Behold, we are my lord’s slaves, both we and he also in whose hand the cup is found.”
en_kjv: And Judah said, What shall we say unto my lord? what shall we speak? or how shall we clear ourselves? God hath found out the iniquity of thy servants: behold, we are my lord’s servants, both we, and he also with whom the cup is found.

tcz: Hinlah Joseph in adonbut in, “Hiche ho chu keiya kon in kigam lhat maihen, keiman bolda jeng inge, hiche pasal pa ka khon kimu doh na pa bou chu kasoh a pang ding, adang se sevang damsel in napa koma nung che tauvin,” ati.
en_web: He said, “Far be it from me that I should do so. The man in whose hand the cup is found, he will be my slave; but as for you, go up in peace to your father.”
en_kjv: And he said, God forbid that I should do so: but the man in whose hand the cup is found, he shall be my servant; and as for you, get you up in peace unto your father.

tcz: Hichun Judah aphei chen aseitai, “Lungset tah in ka pakai koma nasoh pan thu chang khat tou kasei thei ding ham? lungset tah in nei lunghan khum hih in, nangma Pharaoh toh nalal na lhon jong ki bang ahitan;
en_web: Then Judah came near to him, and said, “Oh, my lord, please let your servant speak a word in my lord’s ears, and don’t let your anger burn against your servant; for you are even as Pharaoh.
en_kjv: Then Judah came near unto him, and said, O my lord, let thy servant, I pray thee, speak a word in my lord’s ears, and let not thine anger burn against thy servant: for thou art even as Pharaoh.

tcz: Ka pakai pan phat masa chun nasohte ho nei dong uvin, nangma hon sopi nanei juvem ahiloule na pa'u umnalai em natin,
en_web: My lord asked his servants, saying, ‘Have you a father, or a brother?’
en_kjv: My lord asked his servants, saying, Have ye a father, or a brother?

tcz: Chuin keima hon ka donbut un, henge ka pakai pa ka tiuvin kapa'u jong adam nalaiye ahin amavang ateh lheh tai ka tiuve, chule achapa aneopen pachu ateh jou nungsanga ahin ahi. Asopipa jong athi tan, amabou chu anu sunga hing doh ahin, hijeh a chu apan jong hatah a angailut ahi,” ati.
en_web: We said to my lord, ‘We have a father, an old man, and a child of his old age, a little one; and his brother is dead, and he alone is left of his mother; and his father loves him.’
en_kjv: And we said unto my lord, We have a father, an old man, and a child of his old age, a little one; and his brother is dead, and he alone is left of his mother, and his father loveth him.

tcz: Nangman thu neina peh jal a amapa chu hinpui un keiman kamit taha kamu nom e natin;
en_web: You said to your servants, ‘Bring him down to me, that I may set my eyes on him.’
en_kjv: And thou saidst unto thy servants, Bring him down unto me, that I may set mine eyes upon him.

tcz: Ahin keima hon kana donbut un, ka pakai pa'u chu hiche chapang chun apa adalha thei poi ajeh chu apa thilo thei ahi.
en_web: We said to my lord, ‘The boy can’t leave his father, for if he should leave his father, his father would die.’
en_kjv: And we said unto my lord, The lad cannot leave his father: for if he should leave his father, his father would die.

tcz: Ahin nangman thu neina mop kit un, nasopi pa'u alhum pen pa ahung tokah a nanghon kamai namu kitlou dingu ahitai nati.
en_web: You said to your servants, ‘Unless your youngest brother comes down with you, you will see my face no more.’
en_kjv: And thou saidst unto thy servants, Except your youngest brother come down with you, ye shall see my face no more.

tcz: Hichun keiho kaki nungle un, na sohpa kapa'u kom lang a ka pakai pa uvin thugah na neisei peh hou chu ama koma ka na lhut tauve.
en_web: When we came up to your servant my father, we told him the words of my lord.
en_kjv: And it came to pass when we came up unto thy servant my father, we told him the words of my lord.

tcz: Hichun nalhacha pa kapa uvin hitin aseiye, nangma hon nahe uvin ka loinu Rachel in cha ni eihin peh in ahi.
en_web: Your servant, my father, said to us, ‘You know that my wife bore me two sons.
en_kjv: And thy servant my father said unto us, Ye know that my wife bare me two sons:

tcz: Chule amani lah a khat pa eida lhatan ahung ki nungle tapon; gamsa hon ahal hal a abotel ding in ginmo aum lheh tan, hiche apatna chun tugei hin kamu kha tapoi ati.
en_web: One went out from me, and I said, “Surely he is torn in pieces;” and I haven’t seen him since.
en_kjv: and the one went out from me, and I said, Surely he is torn in pieces; and I saw him not since:

tcz: Tua amapa asopipa hi na puidoh uva boina hahsat na hintoh le tua kasam kan jouva thina lunghem na nei tosah kit diu ahi,’ ati.
en_web: If you take this one also from me, and harm happens to him, you will bring down my gray hairs with sorrow to Sheol.’
en_kjv: and if ye take this also from me, and mischief befall him, ye shall bring down my gray hairs with sorrow to the grave.

tcz: Tun ka pakai keima kapa henga hiche chapang jao lou vin ki nungle thei pong kate ati, ajeh chu kapa'u hinkho le hiche chapang pa hinkho hi aman khom lhon ahiye.
en_web: Now therefore when I come to your servant my father, and the boy is not with us; since his life is bound up in the boy’s life;
en_kjv: Now therefore when I come to thy servant my father, and the lad be not with us; seeing that his life is bound up in the lad’s life;

tcz: Kapan hiche chapang hi amulou le thilo tei ding ahi, nasoh teho hin kapa'u samkan jouva thina kato sah kit dingu ahi tai atiuve.
en_web: it will happen, when he sees that the boy is no more, that he will die. Your servants will bring down the gray hairs of your servant, our father, with sorrow to Sheol.
en_kjv: it shall come to pass, when he seeth that the lad is not with us, that he will die: and thy servants shall bring down the gray hairs of thy servant our father with sorrow to the grave.

tcz: Amonga jong na sohpa hi kapa henga hiche chapang khel'a hung kipe doh jenga hitia hi, keiman ama hi naheng kahin nunglhut kit louva ahile nahenga hinkho lhumkei jin themmo chang jeng ing kate, kati ahi.
en_web: For your servant became collateral for the boy to my father, saying, ‘If I don’t bring him to you, then I will bear the blame to my father forever.’
en_kjv: For thy servant became surety for the lad unto my father, saying, If I bring him not unto thee, then I shall bear the blame to my father for ever.

tcz: Hijeh chu kapu lungset tah in ahithei dingle hiche chapang khel in keima hi nangma soh din um tang kate, chule ahithei dingle hiche chapang hi a u-teho toh ki nungle tau hen.
en_web: Now therefore, please let your servant stay instead of the boy, my lord’s slave; and let the boy go up with his brothers.
en_kjv: Now therefore, I pray thee, let thy servant abide instead of the lad a bondman to my lord; and let the lad go up with his brethren.

tcz: Keima iti kapa koma kaki nungle kit ding ham hiche chapang pa beiya hi ati, kapa in gim genthei athoh ding chu iti kavet jou ding ham ati.
en_web: For how will I go up to my father, if the boy isn’t with me?—lest I see the evil that will come on my father.”
en_kjv: For how shall I go up to my father, and the lad be not with me? lest peradventure I see the evil that shall come on my father.

tcz: Hichun Joseph ana tohkhompi ho masanga ama le ama akitim jou tapon hichun awthong jejun akaptan, mijouse hikoma kon in asoldoh in ama asopi ho lah a akiphong doh tan ahi.
en_web: Then Joseph couldn’t control himself before all those who stood before him, and he called out, “Cause everyone to go out from me!” No one else stood with him, while Joseph made himself known to his brothers.
en_kjv: Then Joseph could not refrain himself before all them that stood by him; and he cried, Cause every man to go out from me. And there stood no man with him, while Joseph made himself known unto his brethren.

tcz: Chuin ama hatah in akaptan ahile Egypt miten jong aja uvin, chule hiche thu kisei chu apet petin Pharaoh in ajatan ahi.
