tcz: Heicha hemlou mang mi chun tha tamtah asuhmang ding ahi, hijeh chun na hei chang kinol phat in. Hiche hi chihna amanlutna ahin, na lolhin sah ding ahi.
en_web: If the ax is blunt, and one doesn’t sharpen the edge, then he must use more strength; but skill brings success.
en_kjv: If the iron be blunt, and he do not whet the edge, then must he put to more strength: but wisdom is profitable to direct.
tcz_gospelgo: Naheicha mol’a nol-hem louvan hatuh a natuh ngai ahi. Thil ijakai gontoh masah chu chihna joh ahi.

tcz: Gul chu na kingai sah kah’a na hin chuh man tahleh ipi phatsah’a gulchu na kingai sah ki got ham?
en_web: If the snake bites before it is charmed, then is there no profit for the charmer’s tongue.
en_kjv: Surely the serpent will bite without enchantment; and a babbler is no better.
tcz_gospelgo: Gul nakihcuh masah sah thei le nagul saithemlo aumpoi.

tcz: Chih thusei ho pachat achanguve, hinlah ngolna thuseiho athusei-uva akipal jiuve.
en_web: The words of a wise man’s mouth are gracious; but a fool is swallowed by his own lips.
en_kjv: The words of a wise man’s mouth are gracious; but the lips of a fool will swallow up himself.
tcz_gospelgo: Michingin thu aseiteng min agin lon, mi-ngol vang aseisaa thi ahibouve.

tcz: Mingol ho lunggel chu ngolhoi thua akipanin, hiti chun athungah lhahnau jong chu gitlouna tah ngolna hung hiding ahi.
en_web: The beginning of the words of his mouth is foolishness; and the end of his talk is mischievous madness.
en_kjv: The beginning of the words of his mouth is foolishness: and the end of his talk is mischievous madness.
tcz_gospelgo: Chapang thu jeng thupat nan aneiyin, ngol thubuh-in achaiye.

tcz: Mingol hon thu aseibe beuvin, khonunga ipi hunglhung ding ahi koiman ahepon, asei chenthei pouvin ahi.
en_web: A fool also multiplies words. Man doesn’t know what will be; and that which will be after him, who can tell him?
en_kjv: A fool also is full of words: a man cannot tell what shall be; and what shall be after him, who can tell him?
tcz_gospelgo: Mi-ngol’in thuchaije helouvin asei sei jengjie. Khonung thilsoh ding koiman ahepon, ithi nung tengu thilsoh ding eihil theiyuva jong koima aumpoi.

tcz: Mingol hon neocha atoh nauva chun athangui pai uvin, in iti hunglhun ding ham tijong akihetji pouve.
en_web: The labor of fools wearies every one of them; for he doesn’t know how to go to the city.
en_kjv: The labour of the foolish wearieth every one of them, because he knoweth not how to go to the city.
tcz_gospelgo: Mi-ngol inlam jotle jong kihet lou mi chu natoh achimvah jin ahi.

tcz: Gamsunga vaihom hon jingpia golvah abolluva, gamsung vaihomma pang soh chu lunghem umtah ahi.
en_web: Woe to you, land, when your king is a child, and your princes eat in the morning!
en_kjv: Woe to thee, O land, when thy king is a child, and thy princes eat in the morning.
tcz_gospelgo: Lengpa achapan behseh a, lamkaiten jan khovah vah agolnop abol teng gamsungin hahsa athoh lo jie.

tcz: Lenga pang milunglen lamkai nei gamsung chule aphatcha golvahbol vaipi popa chu pachat umtah ahi.
en_web: Happy are you, land, when your king is the son of nobles, and your princes eat in due season, for strength, and not for drunkenness!
en_kjv: Blessed art thou, O land, when thy king is the son of nobles, and thy princes eat in due season, for strength, and not for drunkenness.
tcz_gospelgo: Ama chamtah a thu ngahna semdoh thei leng le aphat cha neh le chah kijon thei, kitim them a jukham lou lamkaite neikhaa gamsung chu ahampha ahiuve.

tcz: Mithase inchung chu govatna theijin anem lha suh jin, thaset jeh’a inchung vangchet chut jia ahi.
en_web: By slothfulness the roof sinks in; and through idleness of the hands the house leaks.
en_kjv: By much slothfulness the building decayeth; and through idleness of the hands the house droppeth through.
tcz_gospelgo: Mihem athaset behseh a inchungse lai tholbit nom lou chu, go vantin, in lhuh lo ding ahi.

tcz: Golnop bol hin nuipohlahna asodohjin, lengpitwi jin kipana apei, chule sum in ijakai achojin ahi.
en_web: A feast is made for laughter, and wine makes the life glad; and money is the answer for all things.
en_kjv: A feast is made for laughter, and wine maketh merry: but money answereth all things.
tcz_gospelgo: Golvah hin nakipasah-in, judon hin nalipsah chom nai; ahivangin sum beiyin khat’a khat jong nabol theipoi.

tcz: Lengpa chu imacha louvin gel-hihbeh in, chule athuneipa chu nalupna jenga jong nuisat hih in. Ajeh chu vacha neocha chun nathusei chu agalhutna naseiho chu aseipeh ding ahi.
en_web: Don’t curse the king, no, not in your thoughts; and don’t curse the rich in your bedroom, for a bird of the sky may carry your voice, and that which has wings may tell the matter.
en_kjv: Curse not the king, no not in thy thought; and curse not the rich in thy bedchamber: for a bird of the air shall carry the voice, and that which hath wings shall tell the matter.
tcz_gospelgo: Guh thim hijongle lengpa seiset dan, najalkhun thip sung hijongle mihao chu seise hih-in. Naseidoh chu vacha khat touvin pontin agaseipeh thei ahi.

tcz: Nangman na muchi chu twipi gallam geijin thotdoh in, chule aphatcha a-pungdoh chu nahenga hung le lhun kit ding ahi.
en_web: Cast your bread on the waters; for you shall find it after many days.
en_kjv: Cast thy bread upon the waters: for thou shalt find it after many days.
tcz_gospelgo: Gamchom mito kiveikhom nan sum toh le chun, tu tiphat khat le sumkan namu tei ding ahi.

tcz: Hinlah nangman na sumkhol ho chu mun tampia homjal in, ajeh chu ipi hahsatna in ahinphah ding nangin nahepoi.
en_web: Give a portion to seven, yes, even to eight; for you don’t know what evil will be on the earth.
en_kjv: Give a portion to seven, and also to eight; for thou knowest not what evil shall be upon the earth.
tcz_gospelgo: Muntin gamtin a sum koisoh keiyin, ajeh chu hiche vannoiya hi itobang hamsetna nato ding nakihet masahpoi.

tcz: Meibol kitol atam tengleh, go ahung julha jin ahi. Thingphung chu sahlam hihen lhanglam hijongleh alhuhna’a chun aum den jeng’e.
en_web: If the clouds are full of rain, they empty themselves on the earth; and if a tree falls toward the south, or toward the north, in the place where the tree falls, there shall it be.
en_kjv: If the clouds be full of rain, they empty themselves upon the earth: and if the tree fall toward the south, or toward the north, in the place where the tree falleth, there it shall be.
tcz_gospelgo: Thingphung chu hoilam pen ngan lhu jongle, alhuhnaa chu kijam den jeng ding ahi. Meilhang ajin teng go ajuijie.

tcz: Loubol mi chun gophat pet anga leh chang phutdoh ponte. Meibol kitol avetsui jing uleh , itih in jong chang at pouvinte.
en_web: He who observes the wind won’t sow; and he who regards the clouds won’t reap.
en_kjv: He that observeth the wind shall not sow; and he that regardeth the clouds shall not reap.
tcz_gospelgo: Huile go khophat kito phat ngah a natong louva naumle lho lhung ding neipon nate.

tcz: Nangman huinun na chu alampi na hetdoh theilou tobang'in, ahilouleh naocha anu oisunga kijil chu iti hungkhan let ham ti na het thei lou tobang'in, nangman hiche ho jouse hinbol’a Pathen chaloh dan nahet thei lou ding ahi.
en_web: As you don’t know what is the way of the wind, nor how the bones grow in the womb of her who is with child; even so you don’t know the work of God who does all.
en_kjv: As thou knowest not what is the way of the spirit, nor how the bones do grow in the womb of her that is with child: even so thou knowest not the works of God who maketh all.
tcz_gospelgo: Numei naobu sunga naosen hinkhothah hung kipat nahet thei lou banga thil ijakai sem Pathen natoh thilbolje nahet thei lou ding ahi.

tcz: Jingkah tengleh na muchi kitun lang, ni lhangkai jongleh gunchun ponpan in, ijeh inem itileh hoipenna chu apung ding pen chu hung sohdoh ding ham ti nangman nahe poi.
en_web: In the morning sow your seed, and in the evening don’t withhold your hand; for you don’t know which will prosper, whether this or that, or whether they both will be equally good.
en_kjv: In the morning sow thy seed, and in the evening withhold not thine hand: for thou knowest not whether shall prosper, either this or that, or whether they both shall be alike good.
tcz_gospelgo: Jingkah nilhah-in muchi tun, natulut chan pha, khangdoh doh ding ham, alah a khatseh bou khangdoh ding ham nahepoi.

tcz: Vah hi anom’e! Khovah thah hunglhun vet hi iti lunglhai um hitam?
en_web: Truly the light is sweet, and it is a pleasant thing for the eyes to see the sun.
en_kjv: Truly the light is sweet, and a pleasant thing it is for the eyes to behold the sun:
tcz_gospelgo: Sunlai khovah hi nomsahna dinga nomtah ahi.

tcz: Mi chu ateh geija ahinna ahileh, anitin hinkhoa kipah hen. Chujongleh hinkhoa gimna nikho jong tampi hunglhung ding ahiti jong geldoh uhen. Thil ahung lhungbe dingho hi ajeh bei tobangbep hung hi theija ahi.
en_web: Yes, if a man lives many years, let him rejoice in them all; but let him remember the days of darkness, for they shall be many. All that comes is vanity.
en_kjv: but if a man live many years, and rejoice in them all; yet let him remember the days of darkness; for they shall be many. All that cometh is vanity.
tcz_gospelgo: Nahinkhon kum lhunseh le kipah-in. Itih chan hing jongle chun sot louva nathi ding geldoh jingin. Kinemtah a nga jing ding jong aum sampoi.

tcz: Khangdong ho, khandonlai hi iti kidan hitam! Kipana tothon nalunggil in kihilna nei jing in, na bolnom chan bol lin; nalunggot nalam jousea chelen, chule namit tenin avetthei chan vehen. Ahinlah nathilbol chan chu Pathen henga namopohna hiding ahi, ti geldoh in.
en_web: Rejoice, young man, in your youth, and let your heart cheer you in the days of your youth, and walk in the ways of your heart, and in the sight of your eyes; but know that for all these things God will bring you into judgment.
en_kjv: Rejoice, O young man, in thy youth; and let thy heart cheer thee in the days of thy youth, and walk in the ways of thine heart, and in the sight of thine eyes: but know thou, that for all these things God will bring thee into judgment.
tcz_gospelgo: Vo khangdong, nakhangdon kipapin! Nakhangdon pat’in kipah jingin. Nabolnom nom bol’in, nadei deiyin chonin. Amavnag ipi hile nabol chan chu Pathenin thu natanpeh ding geldoh jingin.

tcz: Hijeh chun lungkhamna kiti bol hih in, chule natahsa damtheina din kichin tup in; chule hiche hi geldoh jing in, khandonlai na masanga na hinkho umsun hi ajehbei tobangbep ahibouve.
en_web: Therefore remove sorrow from your heart, and put away evil from your flesh; for youth and the dawn of life are vanity.
en_kjv: Therefore remove sorrow from thy heart, and put away evil from thy flesh: for childhood and youth are vanity.
tcz_gospelgo: Imacha lung gimpi dan, thoh lel jong nei hih-in. Khangdong sot ding naihpoi.

tcz: Nakhangdonlai thanopna chun na Sempa suhmilna sodoh hih hen. Natehset masang nakhangdon laihin, Ama chu jabollin chule “Hinkho hi anomtapoi,” tin seijin.
en_web: Remember also your Creator in the days of your youth, before the evil days come, and the years draw near, when you will say, “I have no pleasure in them;”
en_kjv: Remember now thy Creator in the days of thy youth, while the evil days come not, nor the years draw nigh, when thou shalt say, I have no pleasure in them;
tcz_gospelgo: “Kahin nomtapoi,” natina ding-ni le lha kum ho hunglhun masang, nakhangdon pet hin Nasempa geldoh jingin!

tcz: Nateh’a namit tenin nisa lha le ahsiho vah avetna athim masang in, chule meibol’a kona go hung ju lha ding van chu athim masangin Ama chu geldoh in.
en_web: Before the sun, the light, the moon, and the stars are darkened, and the clouds return after the rain;
en_kjv: while the sun, or the light, or the moon, or the stars, be not darkened, nor the clouds return after the rain:
tcz_gospelgo: Nateh teng-nisa vah le lha vah, ahsite vah geiyin nang din thimtan tin, namaiya meibol jing tobang dingahi.

tcz: Na in ngah’a pang nakengho chu ahung kithin masang in, na mihat ho alhahsuh uva chule na lengkou teni ahung bon masang in, na Sempa geldoh in. Nasoh um amoh chengse le naha hon ima alhai theilou masang in; chule namit tenin amutheina bangkot, numei hon avetna chu ahung thim masang in, Ama chu geldoh in.
en_web: in the day when the keepers of the house shall tremble, and the strong men shall bow themselves, and the grinders cease because they are few, and those who look out of the windows are darkened,
en_kjv: in the day when the keepers of the house shall tremble, and the strong men shall bow themselves, and the grinders cease because they are few, and those that look out of the windows be darkened,
tcz_gospelgo: Chuteng nakihonna banjangte ni kithingin tin, tua hatna lai nakengte ni hung thabei ding, naha pulsoh a, lhom behseh ding-an nalhaimo ding, namit thim a namu chen thei lou ding ahi:

tcz: Hinkhoa phat kijen naneipat ahung kichai masang in chule natohgim phat ahung kichai masang in, Ama chu geldoh in. Husat ginho ahung thipma chule vacha hamgin najah masat tengleh nangma nahung kithodoh ding ahi.
en_web: and the doors shall be shut in the street; when the sound of the grinding is low, and one shall rise up at the voice of a bird, and all the daughters of music shall be brought low;
en_kjv: and the doors shall be shut in the streets, when the sound of the grinding is low, and he shall rise up at the voice of the bird, and all the daughters of musick shall be brought low;
tcz_gospelgo: Na-ngongin natin, kholai dung husa jatapon nate. Sumheiya chang kigot gin le tumging thei kitum jacheo cheovin natin, ahivangin vacha hamin kinkhangin nate.

tcz: Nangma lhuh ding nahung kichat tijatna, chule lamlen jotna’a jong setto ding nalung khama, vaopah banga nasam ho ahung kana, chule khaokhopi tobanga nakhupboh’a lam nahin jot masang in, chule jitoh kingaina imacha nei talouva nahung um masang in, Ama chu geldoh in. Nangman na tonsot mun na jot masanga, lhankhuh nanai tul tul’a, na kivuina muna lunghem ho aka phat’u hung lhun masang in, Ama chu geldoh in.
en_web: yes, they shall be afraid of heights, and terrors will be on the way; and the almond tree shall blossom, and the grasshopper shall be a burden, and desire shall fail; because man goes to his everlasting home, and the mourners go about the streets;
en_kjv: also when they shall be afraid of that which is high, and fears shall be in the way, and the almond tree shall flourish, and the grasshopper shall be a burden, and desire shall fail: because man goeth to his long home, and the mourners go about the streets:
tcz_gospelgo: Khousang laiya kaldoh ngam pon natin, chele vale jong tijat umtante. Nasem kangin tin, kisuh hei kitouhei hahsa nasah a, imacha lung gul naneilou ding ahitai. Ngahmun jon a che ihitauvin, kholai dunga ka le lunghem umtante.

tcz: Nangma nakhandon pat hin dangka khaogui akibotan masang, sana khon aki vohkeh masang, twinah phunga twibel aki tachip masang, twibel phunga kangtalai aki vohbal masang in, na Sempa geldoh in.
en_web: before the silver cord is severed, or the golden bowl is broken, or the pitcher is broken at the spring, or the wheel broken at the cistern,
en_kjv: or ever the silver cord be loosed, or the golden bowl be broken, or the pitcher be broken at the fountain, or the wheel broken at the cistern.
tcz_gospelgo: Dangla khang kobottan ding sana thaomei hung lhaa keh ding twikul’a twi thalna khao tan a twibel lenglhaa kitatjal ding ahi.

tcz: Ijeh inem itileh hiche phat chu ahung lhunteng, vut leiset kisoh kit intin; chule lhagao chu apepa Pathen henga kile kit ding ahi.
en_web: and the dust returns to the earth as it was, and the spirit returns to God who gave it.
en_kjv: Then shall the dust return to the earth as it was: and the spirit shall return unto God who gave it.
tcz_gospelgo: Itahsapheu leiset’a kile kit’a leivui soh ding, hinna hu hi eipeuva Pathen henga kile kit ding ahi.

tcz: Thuhilpa chun, “Ijakai ajehbei tobangbep ahi, ajeh bei ahisoh keije,” ati.
en_web: “Vanity of vanities,” says the Preacher. “All is vanity!”
en_kjv: Vanity of vanities, saith the Preacher; all is vanity.
tcz_gospelgo: Pannabei seh-in michingthempan aseiyin, aboncha hi pannabei hel’in aseiye.

tcz: Hiche hi nalung in ching jing in: Thuhilpa chu miching ahin, chule amachun ahetchan chu miho ahilji ahi. Ama chun thuchih tampi chingthetah’a angaitoa, agel-a chule ahop khen tohle ahi.
en_web: Further, because the Preacher was wise, he still taught the people knowledge. Yes, he pondered, sought out, and set in order many proverbs.
en_kjv: And moreover, because the Preacher was wise, he still taught the people knowledge; yea, he gave good heed, and sought out, and set in order many proverbs.
tcz_gospelgo: Michingthempa hi achih jal’in mipi chu ahet jouse ahil jing jeng theiye. Thuchihho kihilna aneiyin, adihjeu apatep cheh-e.

tcz: Thuhilpa chun, thudihtah chu mudoh dinga ahol-a thutah chu kichehtah’a aphondoh nom ahi.
en_web: The Preacher sought to find out acceptable words, and that which was written blamelessly, words of truth.
en_kjv: The Preacher sought to find out acceptable words: and that which was written was upright, even words of truth.
tcz_gospelgo: Michingthempan lungmonna thuh holdoh agon, asutdoh thucheng ho hi thu kitah jeng ahi.

tcz: Miching thusei hochu tengcha hemtah tobanga ahin, najongleh phachoma ahi. Athuseiju kilakhom hohi thingkil kikil matchet tobang leuva kelngoi chingpan akelngoi ho huikhomna’a amanchah ji tobang ahi.
en_web: The words of the wise are like goads; and like nails well fastened are words from the masters of assemblies, which are given from one shepherd.
en_kjv: The words of the wise are as goads, and as nails fastened by the masters of assemblies, which are given from one shepherd.
tcz_gospelgo: Michingte thusei ho hi kelngoi chingten kelngoi hoikhomna aman’u tenggol lhoutah tobang ahin, thuchih kidong khom ho jong thilkil’a kikhendet kheh banga umsot ding ahi.Hicheng hi kelngoi chin a Eichingpau Pathen thilpeh ahi.

tcz: Hinlah kacha, Keiman thuhilna naneibe kit inge: Chingthei jin, ajeh chu lekhabu ho jihdoh kitia kichai tih aumpoi, chule lekha hasim hin na cholsah ahije.
en_web: Furthermore, my son, be admonished: of making many books there is no end; and much study is a weariness of the flesh.
en_kjv: And further, by these, my son, be admonished: of making many books there is no end; and much study is a weariness of the flesh.
tcz_gospelgo: Kachapa, kichih theina ding khat auim nalaiye. A-ngahbu ajobu um louva lekha kijih jing ahi, hasim behseh hi nacholsah bep hinte.

tcz: Hiche hi aboncha thu kaigom ahi. Tun keiman thukhumkhana kanei hi ngai phan: Pathen ginna neijin chule athupeh ho jui jin, ajeh chu hiche hi amitakip tohding kin ahi.
en_web: This is the end of the matter. All has been heard. Fear God and keep his commandments; for this is the whole duty of man.
en_kjv: Let us hear the conclusion of the whole matter: Fear God, and keep his commandments: for this is the whole duty of man.
tcz_gospelgo: Hijat kalval hin seibe ding thil khat aum’e: Pathen gingin, athupeh chengse nit’in; ajeh chu hiche dinga hi mihem asemdoh ahi.

tcz: Ijakai chung changa, guhthim thudol- apha hihen ase hijongleh, Pathen in eiho thilbol dungjui cheh’a thutanna anei ding ahi.
en_web: For God will bring every work into judgment, with every hidden thing, whether it is good, or whether it is evil.
en_kjv: For God shall bring every work into judgment, with every secret thing, whether it be good, or whether it be evil.
tcz_gospelgo: Thil ijakai-apha hihen ase hileh, guh thima kibol ho geiya Pathenin ibol ho’u cuhnga ithuu atan cheh ding ahi.

tcz: Zailom: Hiche hi Solomon la ho lah’a apipen, adang jouse sanga thupi ahi.
en_web: The Song of songs, which is Solomon’s.
en_kjv: The song of songs, which is Solomon’s.

tcz: Mounu: Neichop in lang, avel in neichop in, ajeh chu nei deibolna chu lengpitwi sang in jong alhumjoi.
en_web: Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth; for your love is better than wine.
en_kjv: Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth: For thy love is better than wine.

tcz: Gimnamtwi nakinu chu iti namtwija hitam, namin ngei hi agim namtwi kitungdoh tobang ahi. Akidang poi, khangdong nungah jousen hibang loma nahin deiju hi!
en_web: Your oils have a pleasing fragrance. Your name is oil poured out, therefore the virgins love you.
en_kjv: Because of the savour of thy good ointments Thy name is as ointment poured forth, Therefore do the virgins love thee.

tcz: Kei jong neipuijin, hung in; kijam ta hite! Lengpan ajalna pindan’ah ei puilut hen. Zailom: Iti kahin kipapiu hitam, O Lengpa. Na milungset dan hi lengpitwi sang in ka ngaisang jouve. Mounu: Nahin ngaisangnau hi adih tangeiye!
en_web: Take me away with you. Let’s hurry. The king has brought me into his rooms. We will be glad and rejoice in you. We will praise your love more than wine! They are right to love you.
en_kjv: Draw me, we will run after thee: The king hath brought me into his chambers: We will be glad and rejoice in thee, We will remember thy love more than wine: The upright love thee.

tcz: Keima ka vouso avom vang'in kamelhoi nai, Vo Jerusalem Chanute-Cedar phaiya ponbuh kisongho banga vom, Solomon pondal banga vom chu ka hinai.
en_web: I am dark, but lovely, you daughters of Jerusalem, like Kedar’s tents, like Solomon’s curtains.
en_kjv: I am black, but comely, O ye daughters of Jerusalem, As the tents of Kedar, as the curtains of Solomon.

tcz: Kavouso avom jeh-in, Neihin vehih-uvin-nisan ei kahdup jeh ahibouve. Ka sopi pasal ho ka chung ah alunghang uve, alengpi leiju vekol ding in eino uvin, hijeh chun kei le kei ka kijen joupoi; keima lengpilei ka kivet kol man poi.
en_web: Don’t stare at me because I am dark, because the sun has scorched me. My mother’s sons were angry with me. They made me keeper of the vineyards. I haven’t kept my own vineyard.
en_kjv: Look not upon me, because I am black, Because the sun hath looked upon me: My mother’s children were angry with me; They made me the keeper of the vineyards; But mine own vineyard have I not kept.

tcz: Nei seipeh-in, O goldei, tuni na kelngoi honho hoilama na puiding ham? Sun teng hoikoma na kol sah ding ham? Ajeh chu keima hi noti banga naloi-napaiho chule kelngoite lah’a iti ka vavai le jeng thei ding ham?
en_web: Tell me, you whom my soul loves, where you graze your flock, where you rest them at noon; for why should I be as one who is veiled beside the flocks of your companions?
en_kjv: Tell me, O thou whom my soul loveth, Where thou feedest, where thou makest thy flock to rest at noon: For why should I be as one that turneth aside by the flocks of thy companions?

tcz: Moulang: Na het loule, O nungah melhoipen nu; ka kelngoi ho kikaina nung juiyin lang, kelngoi chingho ponbuh vel’a chun na kelchate vah-in.
en_web: If you don’t know, most beautiful among women, follow the tracks of the sheep. Graze your young goats beside the shepherds’ tents.
en_kjv: If thou know not, O thou fairest among women, Go thy way forth by the footsteps of the flock, And feed thy kids beside the shepherds’ tents.

tcz: O ka deinu, na nunnop dan hi Pharaoh sakol lagol lah-a khat toh nabang’e.
en_web: I have compared you, my love, to a steed in Pharaoh’s chariots.
en_kjv: I have compared thee, O my love, To a company of horses in Pharaoh’s chariots.

tcz: Na bengmai alangtoa hi iti deium hitam! Na bilba tenin asal emsel jeng’e! Nangong jong iti dei um hitam, na sana bilba hung kailha chun ajem hoi be cheh-e.
en_web: Your cheeks are beautiful with earrings, your neck with strings of jewels.
en_kjv: Thy cheeks are comely with rows of jewels, Thy neck with chains of gold.

tcz: Zailom: Sanavui sempeh-ungting, kicheina ding dangkavui toh thosah-unge.
en_web: We will make you earrings of gold, with studs of silver.
en_kjv: We will make thee borders of gold With studs of silver.

tcz: Mounu: Lengpa jalkhun chung ah alum in, gimnamtwi ka kinu gimnam hi aki tunglut jel jeng’e.
en_web: While the king sat at his table, my perfume spread its fragrance.
en_kjv: While the king sitteth at his table, My spikenard sendeth forth the smell thereof.

tcz: Ka goldeipa hi ka ang-a Myrrh gim namtwi theineo kikhai abangin ahi.
en_web: My beloved is to me a sachet of myrrh, that lies between my breasts.
en_kjv: A bundle of myrrh is my well-beloved unto me; He shall lie all night betwixt my breasts.

tcz: Ama hi En-gedi lengpileiya henna pahcha-boh toh abange.
en_web: My beloved is to me a cluster of henna blossoms from the vineyards of En Gedi.
en_kjv: My beloved is unto me as a cluster of camphire In the vineyards of En-gedi.

tcz: Moulang: Iti hoiya hoi nahi hitam, O ka goldei nu! Namit teni hi vakho te abang jeng’e.
en_web: Behold, you are beautiful, my love. Behold, you are beautiful. Your eyes are like doves.
en_kjv: Behold, thou art fair, my love; behold, thou art fair; Thou hast doves’ eyes.

tcz: Mounu: Nangma jong na hoi ngeije, O goldei, kam’a seidoh jou hoi hilouvin dei na um nalom’e! Hampa dong nem hiuheo khu i-jalkhun lhon ding in alom e.
en_web: Behold, you are beautiful, my beloved, yes, pleasant; and our couch is verdant.
en_kjv: Behold, thou art fair, my beloved, yea, pleasant: Also our bed is green.

tcz: Namtwi tah Cedar thingbah ho jeng jong i-inkam lhon ding in apang uvin, chahthing ho jeng jong i-insun lhon ding in apang’uve.
en_web: The beams of our house are cedars. Our rafters are firs.
en_kjv: The beams of our house are cedar, And our rafters of fir.

tcz: Mounu: Kei hi Sharon phaichama pahcha chule phaichama lily pah kahi.
en_web: I am a rose of Sharon, a lily of the valleys.
en_kjv: I am the rose of Sharon, And the lily of the valleys.

tcz: Moulang: Ahi ngeije, lingnang lah-a lily aum bang in, nungah khangdong ho lah-a kadei nu aum e.
en_web: As a lily among thorns, so is my love among the daughters.
en_kjv: As the lily among thorns, So is my love among the daughters.

tcz: Mounu: Thei-hon sunga theithup twipen aum bang in, gollhang khangdong lah-in ka dongma pa aum’e. Alimdam noija keima ka touvin, atheiga twitah chu kane’e.
en_web: As the apple tree among the trees of the wood, so is my beloved among the sons. I sat down under his shadow with great delight, his fruit was sweet to my taste.
en_kjv: As the apple tree among the trees of the wood, So is my beloved among the sons. I sat down under his shadow with great delight, And his fruit was sweet to my taste.

tcz: Aman golvahna in dan sung ah ei kilhon lutpin, eikhohsah dan hi akichen lheh jeng’e.
en_web: He brought me to the banquet hall. His banner over me is love.
en_kjv: He brought me to the banqueting house, And his banner over me was love.

tcz: Lengpi theigan nei thahatsah-in lang, theithup gan nei kidodoh sah-in, ijeh-inem itileh keima nangma ngaija haisam pai ding kahi.
en_web: Strengthen me with raisins, refresh me with apples; for I am faint with love.
en_kjv: Stay me with flagons, comfort me with apples: For I am sick of love.

tcz: Aban veilam ka kikhap in, aban jet in eijut lelei.
en_web: His left hand is under my head. His right hand embraces me.
en_kjv: His left hand is under my head, And his right hand doth embrace me.

tcz: Vo Jerusalem chanute, lou jaova sapeng le sakhi min pan’a katem nahiuve; achama ahung kipatdoh ngal lou leh kideina hi nanghon tildoh tho ahilouleh suh-khahtho din got dauvin.
en_web: I adjure you, daughters of Jerusalem, by the roes, or by the hinds of the field, that you not stir up, nor awaken love, until it so desires.
en_kjv: I charge you, O ye daughters of Jerusalem, By the roes, and by the hinds of the field, That ye stir not up, nor awake my love, till he please.

tcz: O, kangai penpa ahung phei gin kajai! Molsang sang ahinlhah-in, alhang alhang ahin lhah-e.
en_web: The voice of my beloved! Behold, he comes, leaping on the mountains, skipping on the hills.
en_kjv: The voice of my beloved! behold, he cometh Leaping upon the mountains, skipping upon the hills.

tcz: Kangaipa hi man-gangtah sapeng gol tobang le sakhi chalgol tobang ahi. Veuvin, bangtom ah khun ama ading in; bangkot vangkah-a kon in ahin ven, pindan sung ahin velhin ahi.
en_web: My beloved is like a roe or a young deer. Behold, he stands behind our wall! He looks in at the windows. He glances through the lattice.
en_kjv: My beloved is like a roe or a young hart: Behold, he standeth behind our wall, He looketh forth at the windows, Shewing himself through the lattice.

tcz: Kangaipan aseije, “Kithouvin, ngainu! Hiti hin kijot mang ta hite, O melhoi!
en_web: My beloved spoke, and said to me, “Rise up, my love, my beautiful one, and come away.
en_kjv: My beloved spake, and said unto me, Rise up, my love, my fair one, and come away.

tcz: Ven, phalbi a kichai tai; chule gojuh jong atang tai.
en_web: For behold, the winter is past. The rain is over and gone.
en_kjv: For lo, the winter is past, The rain is over and gone;

tcz: Pahchate ahung jamdoh tauvin, vachate mao jinjen lai phat kum kihei ahung lhung tan, vahui hamgin in ikom-ivel khohui alodim tai.
en_web: The flowers appear on the earth. The time of the singing has come, and the voice of the turtledove is heard in our land.
en_kjv: The flowers appear on the earth; The time of the singing of birds is come, And the voice of the turtle is heard in our land;

tcz: Theichang aga pantan, chule lengpipah gimvui akitung tai. Thouvin, ngainu! Hung in gavahdoh hite, O melhoi!”
en_web: The fig tree ripens her green figs. The vines are in blossom. They give out their fragrance. Arise, my love, my beautiful one, and come away.”
en_kjv: The fig tree putteth forth her green figs, And the vines with the tender grape give a good smell. Arise, my love, my fair one, and come away.

tcz: Moulang: Kol song panga songpi khi kah-ah kavakhu akiselle. Na somai nei musah-in, na awgin nei jahsah in. Ajeh chu na awgin angeiyin, na somai ahoi ngeije.
en_web: My dove in the clefts of the rock, in the hiding places of the mountainside, let me see your face. Let me hear your voice; for your voice is sweet and your face is lovely.
en_kjv: O my dove, that art in the clefts of the rock, in the secret places of the stairs, Let me see thy countenance, let me hear thy voice; For sweet is thy voice, and thy countenance is comely.

tcz: Zailom: Sealte khu man uvin, khuche sealneo ho khun kingailutna lengpilei laidung ahin chilthang masang uvin, man uvin, ijeh-inem itileh lengpithei pahlai ahitai!
en_web: Catch for us the foxes, the little foxes that plunder the vineyards; for our vineyards are in blossom.
en_kjv: Take us the foxes, The little foxes, that spoil the vines: For our vines have tender grapes.

tcz: Mounu: Ka ngailutpa hi keija ahi in, keima ama-a kahi. Aman kelngoite Lily pahho lah-in alhajin, avahva ji’e.
en_web: My beloved is mine, and I am his. He browses among the lilies.
en_kjv: My beloved is mine, and I am his: He feedeth among the lilies.

tcz: Khovahkon huilhi ahung nun masang, chule jan muthim lim jong akihei mang masang in, ka heng hin jon kit in; O ka ngai goldei, Bether lhangdunga sa peng gol ahilouleh sakhi chalgol hunglhai bangchan hung kit teijin.
en_web: Until the day is cool, and the shadows flee away, turn, my beloved, and be like a roe or a young deer on the mountains of Bether.
en_kjv: Until the day break, and the shadows flee away, Turn, my beloved, And be thou like a roe or a young hart Upon the mountains of Bether.

tcz: Mounu: Jan khat khun chunga sa-mang kajal laijin, ka goldeipa ka lhangai lheh-e. Kalhangai lheh jeng in, hinlah ama ahung poi.
en_web: By night on my bed, I sought him whom my soul loves. I sought him, but I didn’t find him.
en_kjv: By night on my bed I sought him whom my soul loveth: I sought him, but I found him not.

tcz: Hijeh chun, “Keima kithoudoh-ing katin khopi tolsungah vahle in, lamlen-lamkah ningkoi jouse ah ka goldeipa gahol le inge,” tin ka kigel tai. Hiti chun ka gahol le in, hinlah ka gamu joupoi.
en_web: I will get up now, and go about the city; in the streets and in the squares I will seek him whom my soul loves. I sought him, but I didn’t find him.
en_kjv: I will rise now, and go about the city In the streets and in the broad ways, I will seek him whom my soul loveth: I sought him, but I found him not.

tcz: Kholai vengtup jan khongah hon lamkah-a eina khamtang uvin, chuin keiman amaho jah-a, “Ka goldeipa chu namu khah uvem?” tin kadong’e.
en_web: The watchmen who go about the city found me; “Have you seen him whom my soul loves?”
en_kjv: The watchmen that go about the city found me: To whom I said, Saw ye him whom my soul loveth?

tcz: Amaho ka dalhah jouchet’na ka goldeipa kamu-mu chun, ka nailut in ka tuhchah jeng tan, chuin kapenna indan, kanu insung ah ka puilut tai.
en_web: I had scarcely passed from them, when I found him whom my soul loves. I held him, and would not let him go, until I had brought him into my mother’s house, into the room of her who conceived me.
en_kjv: It was but a little that I passed from them, But I found him whom my soul loveth: I held him, and would not let him go, Until I had brought him into my mother’s house, And into the chamber of her that conceived me.

tcz: Vo Jerusalem chanute, loujaova sapeng le sakhi min pan’a katem nahiuve; achama ahung kipatdoh ngal lou leh kideina hi nanghon tildoh tho ding le suhkhah-tho din got dauvin.
en_web: I adjure you, daughters of Jerusalem, by the roes, or by the hinds of the field, that you not stir up nor awaken love, until it so desires.
en_kjv: I charge you, O ye daughters of Jerusalem, By the roes, and by the hinds of the field, That ye stir not up, nor awake my love, till he please.

tcz: Zailom: Ipi hitantem hiche gamthip lama kon’a meikhu lom banga kijel doh letlut pi khu? Ipi hitan tem Myrrh gim namtwi chule sumkol veiho gimnamtwi kilhut nam bang jeng hi?
en_web: Who is this who comes up from the wilderness like pillars of smoke, perfumed with myrrh and frankincense, with all spices of the merchant?
en_kjv: Who is this that cometh out of the wilderness like pillars of smoke, Perfumed with myrrh and frankincense, With all powders of the merchant?

tcz: Veuvin, hiche khu Solomon khunjon ahi in, avengtup din Israel sunga gamngah-galsat son-um pen pasal thahat somgup in ahin jui uve.
en_web: Behold, it is Solomon’s carriage! Sixty mighty men are around it, of the mighty men of Israel.
en_kjv: Behold his bed, which is Solomon’s; Threescore valiant men are about it, Of the valiant of Israel.

tcz: Amaho khu chemjam peithem cheh, galsat them cheh ahiuve. Chemjam a kiko sohkei uvin, janteng koiyin lengpa hin bulu jongleh avengdoh ding sadema kimansa ahiuve.
en_web: They all handle the sword, and are expert in war. Every man has his sword on his thigh, because of fear in the night.
en_kjv: They all hold swords, being expert in war: Every man hath his sword upon his thigh because of fear in the night.

tcz: Leng Solomon loupitah-a akijonna khunjon hi Lebanon gam'a thing phapen’a kisem ahi.
en_web: King Solomon made himself a carriage of the wood of Lebanon.
en_kjv: King Solomon made himself a chariot of the wood of Lebanon.

tcz: Akhun jon akhom-ajol chengse chu dangka jeng in a kisem in, achung khu khu sana songmantam in akitom in, apondal-ho chu pon san dup val lheng ahi. Hichu Jerusalem chanu ten ngailutna jouse puma ajep-hoisel’u khunjon ahi.
en_web: He made its pillars of silver, its bottom of gold, its seat of purple, the middle of it being paved with love, from the daughters of Jerusalem.
en_kjv: He made the pillars thereof of silver, The bottom thereof of gold, The covering of it of purple, The midst thereof being paved with love, for the daughters of Jerusalem.

tcz: Mounu: Vo Jerusalem chanute, hung uvin lang Leng Solomon hi hung ve tem’un. Aman akipa thanop napen, ajinei nia anun lallukhuh apeh chu akikhuh-in ahi.
en_web: Go out, you daughters of Zion, and see King Solomon, with the crown with which his mother has crowned him, in the day of his weddings, in the day of the gladness of his heart.
en_kjv: Go forth, O ye daughters of Zion, and behold king Solomon With the crown wherewith his mother crowned him In the day of his espousals, And in the day of the gladness of his heart.

tcz: Moulang: Namelhoi ngeije, ngainu, seidoh jou hoi hilouvin nahoi ngeije. Na ponlukhuh noija namit teni vakhu abang jeng’e. Nasam kailha jong Gilead lhang dunga kon kel-hon hung kijot suh abang jeng’e.
en_web: Behold, you are beautiful, my love. Behold, you are beautiful. Your eyes are like doves behind your veil. Your hair is as a flock of goats, that descend from Mount Gilead.
en_kjv: Behold, thou art fair, my love; behold, thou art fair; Thou hast doves’ eyes within thy locks: Thy hair is as a flock of goats, that appear from mount Gilead.

tcz: Naha ho kelngoi kihet ngousel jouchet’na kisop thengsel bang in akangleh jeng’e. Na mehiuheo dan nolnabei ahin, na hatu jouse jong akigol khom dildel uve.
en_web: Your teeth are like a newly shorn flock, which have come up from the washing, where every one of them has twins. None is bereaved among them.
en_kjv: Thy teeth are like a flock of sheep that are even shorn, which came up from the washing; Whereof every one beareth twins, and none is barren among them.

tcz: Nane geiteni jong patsandup abangin, nakam jeng jong mihiptah ahi. Na bengmai langto jong na ponlukhuh noijah kolbuthei chang asan jit jet abang jenge.
en_web: Your lips are like scarlet thread. Your mouth is lovely. Your temples are like a piece of a pomegranate behind your veil.
en_kjv: Thy lips are like a thread of scarlet, and thy speech is comely: Thy temples are like a piece of a pomegranate within thy locks.

tcz: Na ngongchang jong David insang, migal-hang asang aja galmanchah-omphoa kijem pah jeng toh abangin avet-hoi ngeije.
en_web: Your neck is like David’s tower built for an armory, on which a thousand shields hang, all the shields of the mighty men.
en_kjv: Thy neck is like the tower of David Builded for an armoury, Whereon there hang a thousand bucklers, all shields of mighty men.

tcz: Na-ang teni jong sapengnou teni, Lily pah lah-a lhale sapengnou pengkop teni abange.
en_web: Your two breasts are like two fawns that are twins of a roe, which feed among the lilies.
en_kjv: Thy two breasts are like two young roes that are twins, Which feed among the lilies.

tcz: Khovahkon huilhi nun masang, jan muthim lim kiheimang masang ah; keiman Myrrh molsang kajot’na, bego lhangdung ka jot touding ahitai.
en_web: Until the day is cool, and the shadows flee away, I will go to the mountain of myrrh, to the hill of frankincense.
en_kjv: Until the day break, and the shadows flee away, I will get me to the mountain of myrrh, and to the hill of frankincense.

tcz: Nangma na pumpin nahoije, ngainu, na hoi chamkim ngeiye.
en_web: You are all beautiful, my love. There is no spot in you.
en_kjv: Thou art all fair, my love; there is no spot in thee.

tcz: Lebanon’a kon in neihin juiyin, ka deilhennu, neihin jui tan Lebanon’a kon in. Senir le Hermon molvum, keipi-bahkai ho kokhuh umna lah, Kei-ahsite chenna lhang, hin juisuh-in Amana Molsanga kon’in hung kumsuh tan.
en_web: Come with me from Lebanon, my bride, with me from Lebanon. Look from the top of Amana, from the top of Senir and Hermon, from the lions’ dens, from the mountains of the leopards.
en_kjv: Come with me from Lebanon, my spouse, with me from Lebanon: Look from the top of Amana, from the top of Shenir and Hermon, From the lions’ dens, from the mountains of the leopards.

tcz: Nang in ka lungsung na lodim in, ka goulu nahi, kangai ka jiding nu. Na khivui val emsel toh namit-ha’a neivet dan in ei hentang den jeng tai.
en_web: You have ravished my heart, my sister, my bride. You have ravished my heart with one of your eyes, with one chain of your neck.
en_kjv: Thou hast ravished my heart, my sister, my spouse; Thou hast ravished my heart with one of thine eyes, With one chain of thy neck.

tcz: Nei ngailutnan ei kipa thanop sah-e, ka goulu nahi; ka ngai kaji ding nu. Nei ngaina hi lengpitwi sang in alhumjon, na gimnamtwi hi pahnamtwi sang in jong atwi joi.
en_web: How beautiful is your love, my sister, my bride! How much better is your love than wine, the fragrance of your perfumes than all kinds of spices!
en_kjv: How fair is thy love, my sister, my spouse! How much better is thy love than wine! And the smell of thine ointments than all spices!

tcz: Na negei teni khoiju sang in alhum joi, O ka ji ding nu. Nalei noija khoiju le bongnoi aume. Na von jouse jong Lebanon lhangpah gimtwi anam’e.
en_web: Your lips, my bride, drip like the honeycomb. Honey and milk are under your tongue. The smell of your garments is like the smell of Lebanon.
en_kjv: Thy lips, O my spouse, drop as the honeycomb: Honey and milk are under thy tongue; And the smell of thy garments is like the smell of Lebanon.

tcz: Nangma hi keija ding monga pahcha lei, goulu, chongmou chule khal laiya twinah kiselguh tobang nahi.
en_web: My sister, my bride, is a locked up garden; a locked up spring, a sealed fountain.
en_kjv: A garden inclosed is my sister, my spouse; A spring shut up, a fountain sealed.

tcz: Na pheichung jong kolbuthei toh muinam kikhat tah henna,
en_web: Your shoots are an orchard of pomegranates, with precious fruits, henna with spikenard plants,
en_kjv: Thy plants are an orchard of pomegranates, with pleasant fruits; Camphire, with spikenard,

tcz: Chule leipah namtwi toh sehlhum, kolju le thingthal, bego le Myrhh, aloe le muinam jouse dinga kingapna ahi.
en_web: spikenard and saffron, calamus and cinnamon, with every kind of incense tree; myrrh and aloes, with all the best spices,
en_kjv: Spikenard and saffron; Calamus and cinnamon, with all trees of frankincense; Myrrh and aloes, with all the chief spices:

tcz: Nangma honlei twinah, twichim twikul; Lebanon lhanga kon hung longlha tobang nahi.
en_web: a fountain of gardens, a well of living waters, flowing streams from Lebanon.
en_kjv: A fountain of gardens, a well of living waters, And streams from Lebanon.

tcz: Mounu: Khang in, Sahlam khohui! thouvin, lhanglam khohui! Ka honlei jon ah hung nung in lang akimvel jouse agimtwi hi lhutsohhel tan. O ka goldeipa, na honleija hin hunglut in lang, theiga hoipen hung kilon lang, hung nen.
en_web: Awake, north wind, and come, you south! Blow on my garden, that its spices may flow out. Let my beloved come into his garden, and taste his precious fruits.
en_kjv: Awake, O north wind; and come thou south; Blow upon my garden, that the spices thereof may flow out. Let my beloved come into his garden, And eat his pleasant fruits.

tcz: Moulang: Keima ka kallha luttai ka honlei, kagoulu, kajidinu komah! Keiman Myrrh toh amuinam theiho ka chomkhom in, ka khoiphanga khoiju ka chop’e. Ka lengpitwi toh bongnoi ka don’e.
en_web: I have come into my garden, my sister, my bride. I have gathered my myrrh with my spice; I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey; I have drunk my wine with my milk. Eat, friends! Drink, yes, drink abundantly, beloved.
en_kjv: I am come into my garden, my sister, my spouse: I have gathered my myrrh with my spice; I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey; I have drunk my wine with my milk: Eat, O friends; drink, yea, drink abundantly, O beloved.

tcz: Zailom: O goldei le ngai umte, neuvin lang, don un! Henge, ngailutna hi donkham vaset un.
en_web: I was asleep, but my heart was awake. It is the voice of my beloved who knocks: “Open to me, my sister, my love, my dove, my undefiled; for my head is filled with dew, and my hair with the dampness of the night.”
en_kjv: I sleep, but my heart waketh: It is the voice of my beloved that knocketh saying, Open to me, my sister, my love, my dove, my undefiled: For my head is filled with dew, And my locks with the drops of the night.

tcz: Kangai penpan kot chu ahin hong gotan, hichun ka lung thathou lheh jeng tai.
en_web: My beloved thrust his hand in through the latch opening. My heart pounded for him.
en_kjv: My beloved put in his hand by the hole of the door, And my bowels were moved for him.

tcz: Keiman ka dongmapa kot honpeh ding in thanom tah in ka chomdoh-in, ka khut chung ah jong gimnamtwi kavatnatsah-in ahi. Ka khut jung Myrrh gimtwija chun kotkil chu kahong tan ahi.
en_web: I rose up to open for my beloved. My hands dripped with myrrh, my fingers with liquid myrrh, on the handles of the lock.
en_kjv: I rose up to open to my beloved; And my hands dropped with myrrh, And my fingers with sweet smelling myrrh, Upon the handles of the lock.

tcz: Kangai penpa din kot kahonpeh tan, hinlah ama anaum tapoi! Kalung lhadah del jeng tai. Ama holnan kadahlen, hinlah kamu jouta poi. Ka koule-in hinlah adonbutna awgin akija tapoi.
en_web: I opened to my beloved; but my beloved left, and had gone away. My heart went out when he spoke. I looked for him, but I didn’t find him. I called him, but he didn’t answer.
en_kjv: I opened to my beloved; But my beloved had withdrawn himself, and was gone: My soul failed when he spake: I sought him, but I could not find him; I called him, but he gave me no answer.

tcz: Janlaija khongah hon khosung avel le laijun eihung mudoh-un, eijep pop chetchut jeng un, ka ponlukhuh eihodoh peh-un ahi.
en_web: The watchmen who go about the city found me. They beat me. They bruised me. The keepers of the walls took my cloak away from me.
en_kjv: The watchmen that went about the city found me, They smote me, they wounded me; The keepers of the walls took away my vail from me.

tcz: Vo Jerusalem chanute, katem nahiuve-kadongmapa na kimupi khah bang uleh, ama lhangai nan ka tahsa akem lheh jeng tai tihi neina seipeh tauvin.
en_web: I adjure you, daughters of Jerusalem, If you find my beloved, that you tell him that I am faint with love.
en_kjv: I charge you, O daughters of Jerusalem, If ye find my beloved, that ye tell him, That I am sick of love.

tcz: Zailom: Idinga na dongma pachu midang jouse sanga dei um chomdeh hija ham, O melhoi kidang lanu? Ipin na dongma pachu atumbeh-a alulsah chom hija keihon nei temnau chu ka nun diu ham?
en_web: How is your beloved better than another beloved, you fairest among women? How is your beloved better than another beloved, that you do so adjure us?
en_kjv: What is thy beloved more than another beloved, O thou fairest among women? What is thy beloved more than another beloved, that thou dost so charge us?

tcz: Mounu: Kangai penpa chu donghoisel in avouso ajolsel in, aemsel jeng in, midang asang-aja sang in ahoijoi.
en_web: My beloved is white and ruddy. The best among ten thousand.
en_kjv: My beloved is white and ruddy, The chiefest among ten thousand.

tcz: Alujang chu songmantam sang in ahoijon, asam jang va-ah vom bang in avom’e.
en_web: His head is like the purest gold. His hair is bushy, black as a raven.
en_kjv: His head is as the most fine gold, His locks are bushy, and black as a raven.

tcz: Amit teni khaltwi panga tou vakhu bang in aval lheng in, sana khiba bongnoitwi-a kisop ngimsel tobang ahi.
en_web: His eyes are like doves beside the water brooks, washed with milk, mounted like jewels.
en_kjv: His eyes are as the eyes of doves by the rivers of waters, Washed with milk, and fitly set.

tcz: Abengmai chu muinampah honlei, gimtwi hinlhut dohji tobang khu ahi. Ane geiteni jong Lily pah Myrrh gimtwi kichap khum tobang ahi.
en_web: His cheeks are like a bed of spices with towers of perfumes. His lips are like lilies, dropping liquid myrrh.
en_kjv: His cheeks are as a bed of spices, as sweet flowers: His lips like lilies, dropping sweet smelling myrrh.

tcz: Abanjang jong sana pum kihehkol’a sana pahjema kijempol bangin alhanlhaije. Atahsa pum saiha kinotval lhenga, Sapphire songa ki tomjol toh abang’e.
en_web: His hands are like rings of gold set with beryl. His body is like ivory work overlaid with sapphires.
en_kjv: His hands are as gold rings set with the beryl: His belly is as bright ivory overlaid with sapphires.

tcz: Akengteni jong sana khomtoa kon kitungdoh ngunsong khom abang’e. Atahsa gongso adingchah-in, Lebanon lhang bang in ahuikaijin, alhang lehvuma Cedar thing huikai abang’e.
en_web: His legs are like pillars of marble set on sockets of fine gold. His appearance is like Lebanon, excellent as the cedars.
en_kjv: His legs are as pillars of marble, set upon sockets of fine gold: His countenance is as Lebanon, excellent as the cedars.

tcz: Akamsung alhum in, imalam jousea dei umtah chu ahi. Vo Jerusalem chanute, ka ngaipen; ka goldei chu hitobang chu ahi.
en_web: His mouth is sweetness; yes, he is altogether lovely. This is my beloved, and this is my friend, daughters of Jerusalem.
en_kjv: His mouth is most sweet: yea, he is altogether lovely. This is my beloved, and this is my friend, O daughters of Jerusalem.

tcz: Zailom: Nagoldei hoiya che hitam, O melhoi kidang lanu? Nahin holpeh-uvinge, nei seipeh’un hoilam ajot ham?
en_web: Where has your beloved gone, you fairest among women? Where has your beloved turned, that we may seek him with you?
en_kjv: Whither is thy beloved gone, O thou fairest among women? Whither is thy beloved turned aside? that we may seek him with thee.

tcz: Mounu: Kagoldeipa muinam theiho pahna ahonleijah akumsuh tai, hon leilaija akelngoite vahding le Lily pahho loukhom ding in.
en_web: My beloved has gone down to his garden, to the beds of spices, to pasture his flock in the gardens, and to gather lilies.
en_kjv: My beloved is gone down into his garden, to the beds of spices, To feed in the gardens, and to gather lilies.

tcz: Keima ka ngaipenpa-a kahin, ama keija ahi. Ama akelngoi Lily pah lah’a avah-e.
en_web: I am my beloved’s, and my beloved is mine. He browses among the lilies.
en_kjv: I am my beloved’s, and my beloved is mine: He feedeth among the lilies.

tcz: Moulang: Ngainu, namelhoi ngeije, vetnom umtah Tirzah khopi, Jerusalem tobang’in na hoijin; galsat-galhang hon ponlap akidop bang uvin na thupi-e.
en_web: You are beautiful, my love, as Tirzah, lovely as Jerusalem, awesome as an army with banners.
en_kjv: Thou art beautiful, O my love, as Tirzah, Comely as Jerusalem, Terrible as an army with banners.

tcz: Namit tenin avet nalang heiphei jin, ijeh-inem itileh na hoinan haisa mo in eilhai. Nasam kailha jong Gilead lhangdunga kon kel-hon hung kijotsuh abang jeng’e.
en_web: Turn away your eyes from me, for they have overcome me. Your hair is like a flock of goats, that lie along the side of Gilead.
en_kjv: Turn away thine eyes from me, for they have overcome me: Thy hair is as a flock of goats that appear from Gilead.

tcz: Naha ho kelngoi kihet ngousel jouchet’na kisop thengsel bang in akangleh jeng’e. Na mehiuheo dan nolnabei ahi in, na hatu jouse jong akigolkhom dildel uve.
en_web: Your teeth are like a flock of ewes, which have come up from the washing, of which every one has twins; not one is bereaved among them.
en_kjv: Thy teeth are as a flock of sheep which go up from the washing, Whereof every one beareth twins, and there is not one barren among them.

tcz: Na bengmai langto jong na ponlukhuh noijah kolbuthei chang asan jitjet abang jeng’e.
en_web: Your temples are like a piece of a pomegranate behind your veil.
en_kjv: As a piece of a pomegranate are thy temples within thy locks.

tcz: Lengnu somgup, thaikem somget chule sim’a simsenlou nungah khangdong aum in,
en_web: There are sixty queens, eighty concubines, and virgins without number.
en_kjv: There are threescore queens, and fourscore concubines, And virgins without number.

tcz: Hijeng jongleh kenvang ka vakho, achamkim pen nu-anun adeilhen pen, ahing nun dottah’a angailut pen nu bou hi ka deilhen pen’e. Nungah khangdong hon jong angai sang uvin, lengnu tamtah le leng inpia thaikemho jeng in jong ngaisang nan ala choijun:
en_web: My dove, my perfect one, is unique. She is her mother’s only daughter. She is the favorite one of her who bore her. The daughters saw her, and called her blessed. The queens and the concubines saw her, and they praised her.
en_kjv: My dove, my undefiled is but one; She is the only one of her mother, She is the choice one of her that bare her. The daughters saw her, and blessed her; Yea, the queens and the concubines, and they praised her.

tcz: “Koi hija ham, taikho vah banga hung vahdoh-a, chollha banga vet-hoi lheh jenga, nisa banga vah emsela, galsat ho ponlap dop banga gimnei jeng hi?” atiuvin ahi.
en_web: Who is she who looks out as the morning, beautiful as the moon, clear as the sun, and awesome as an army with banners?
en_kjv: Who is she that looketh forth as the morning, Fair as the moon, clear as the sun, And terrible as an army with banners?

tcz: Mounu: Kei jong ka kumsuh-e beleija bepah veding le phaichama hamhing hung dondoh thahho veding, chule lengpigui ho dondoh soh tam, kolbutheiho jong pahsoh hitam ti gave lha ding in.
en_web: I went down into the nut tree grove, to see the green plants of the valley, to see whether the vine budded, and the pomegranates were in flower.
en_kjv: I went down into the garden of nuts to see the fruits of the valley, And to see whether the vine flourished, and the pomegranates budded.

tcz: Hinlah keiman ka kigeldoh masang in, ka lhangai mama jeng na lungthim chun eipui lut tai; keidia milalpa sakol kangtol sung ah.
en_web: Without realizing it, my desire set me with my royal people’s chariots.
en_kjv: Or ever I was aware, My soul made me like the chariots of Ammi-nadib.

tcz: Moulang: Kengdap in adap na keng teni chu iti vetnom um hitam, O leng nungahnu! Na khelphe jol silsel teni jong sana pah jem abang jeng in, khut them tahho suitoh sel abang jeng’e.
en_web: How beautiful are your feet in sandals, prince’s daughter! Your rounded thighs are like jewels, the work of the hands of a skillful workman.
en_kjv: How beautiful are thy feet with shoes, O prince’s daughter! The joints of thy thighs are like jewels, The work of the hands of a cunning workman.

tcz: Na laimu jong lengpitwi kihalkhom kikholna lhengkam bempel tobang ahi. Na oi jong suhlou changphal kisea, Lily pahhoijin aum kim sohkei abang’e.
en_web: Your body is like a round goblet, no mixed wine is wanting. Your waist is like a heap of wheat, set about with lilies.
en_kjv: Thy navel is like a round goblet, which wanteth not liquor: Thy belly is like a heap of wheat set about with lilies.

tcz: Na-ang teni jong apengkop sapeng nou teni tobang ahi.
en_web: Your two breasts are like two fawns, that are twins of a roe.
en_kjv: Thy two breasts are like two young roes that are twins.

tcz: Na ngongchang jong saiha insong kitung tobang ahi. Namit teni jong Bath-rabbim kelkot panga Heshbon twikul chim sitset le val litlet toh abang’e. Na nahlhong jong Damascus lam galdot phahna Lebanon insang bang in ahoisel jeng’e.
en_web: Your neck is like an ivory tower. Your eyes are like the pools in Heshbon by the gate of Bathrabbim. Your nose is like the tower of Lebanon which looks toward Damascus.
en_kjv: Thy neck is as a tower of ivory; Thine eyes like the fishpools in Heshbon, by the gate of Bath-rabbim: Thy nose is as the tower of Lebanon which looketh toward Damascus.

tcz: Na luchang Carmel Molsang bang in akikhang sang in, na samjol val litlet chun lalna le loupina atahlang’e. Na samlom hoije chun lengpa jong chatmo in alhatai.
en_web: Your head on you is like Carmel. The hair of your head like purple. The king is held captive in its tresses.
en_kjv: Thine head upon thee is like Carmel, And the hair of thine head like purple; The king is held in the galleries.

tcz: O, iti hoiya hoi nahi hitam! Iti lunglhaium nahi hitam, ngainu, lunglhainan na dim jeng’e!
en_web: How beautiful and how pleasant you are, love, for delights!
en_kjv: How fair and how pleasant art thou, O love, for delights!

tcz: Na gongso tumthing bang in napai jitjet in, na-ang teni jong aphung’a aga lomho abang’e.
en_web: This, your stature, is like a palm tree, your breasts like its fruit.
en_kjv: This thy stature is like to a palm tree, And thy breasts to clusters of grapes.

tcz: Keiman kaseije, “Aphunga ka kaltouva, atheiga ho ka tuhchah ding ahi.” Na-ang teni lengpithei lom bang hen lang, na haihu theithup gimtwi bang in namtwi hen.
en_web: I said, “I will climb up into the palm tree. I will take hold of its fruit.” Let your breasts be like clusters of the vine, the smell of your breath like apples.
en_kjv: I said, I will go up to the palm tree, I will take hold of the boughs thereof: Now also thy breasts shall be as clusters of the vine, And the smell of thy nose like apples;

tcz: Na michop dan jong lengpitwi twipen akidon teng, ilei chung le i-ha kahlah’a nal-heova alonlut bang in thanop umhen.
en_web: Your mouth is like the best wine, that goes down smoothly for my beloved, gliding through the lips of those who are asleep.
en_kjv: And the roof of thy mouth like the best wine, For my beloved, that goeth down sweetly, Causing the lips of those that are asleep to speak.

tcz: Mounu: Keima ka ngaipenpa-a kahi in, aman jong kei hi ama-a mong in eigel’e.
en_web: I am my beloved’s. His desire is toward me.
en_kjv: I am my beloved’s, and his desire is towards me.

tcz: Hung in, goldei, jaolah-a gavahdoh hitin; gammang-pahchaho lah’a jankho gamang khom hite.
en_web: Come, my beloved! Let’s go out into the field. Let’s lodge in the villages.
en_kjv: Come, my beloved, let us go forth into the field; Let us lodge in the villages.

tcz: Kithou dohvah hitin lengpileija gache hitin, lengpiguiho pah hitam gave hitin; apahmum ho chu ana pahlhasoh hitam, kolbutheiho jong ana pahlhasoh hitam gave hite. Chuteng ka ngailutna ka musah ding nahi.
en_web: Let’s go early up to the vineyards. Let’s see whether the vine has budded, its blossom is open, and the pomegranates are in flower. There I will give you my love.
en_kjv: Let us get up early to the vineyards; Let us see if the vine flourish, whether the tender grape appear, And the pomegranates bud forth: There will I give thee my loves.

tcz: Joldei-ai gimvui nam aki tung in, thei phapenho jong in kotbul ahin phatan; kipa thanopna athah hihen alui hijongleh, nang ding in kana khol khomsoh kei tan ahi, O goldei.
en_web: The mandrakes produce fragrance. At our doors are all kinds of precious fruits, new and old, which I have stored up for you, my beloved.
en_kjv: The mandrakes give a smell, And at our gates are all manner of pleasant fruits, New and old, Which I have laid up for thee, O my beloved.

tcz: Mounu: Kasopi pasal, kanu noitwija kivahdohpa chu ana hile chun ka titave! Chutileh hoikom hihen, koiyin eihin ve jongleh nahin chop jing thei ing kating, koiman jong ei seise thei ponte.
en_web: Oh that you were like my brother, who nursed from the breasts of my mother! If I found you outside, I would kiss you; yes, and no one would despise me.
en_kjv: O that thou wert as my brother, that sucked the breasts of my mother! When I should find thee without, I would kiss thee; Yea, I should not be despised.

tcz: Chuteng neolaija ka chennau in ah napui ing-katin, kideije ki kihil tante. Hichea chun muinam thet lengpitwi na donsah ingting, ka kolbuthei jutwi lhum jet chu ka donsah ding nahi.
en_web: I would lead you, bringing you into the house of my mother, who would instruct me. I would have you drink spiced wine, of the juice of my pomegranate.
en_kjv: I would lead thee, and bring thee into my mother’s house, who would instruct me: I would cause thee to drink of spiced wine, of the juice of my pomegranate.

tcz: Naban veilang ka lukhap hintin, naban jet lang in eikoi tante.
en_web: His left hand would be under my head. His right hand would embrace me.
en_kjv: His left hand should be under my head, And his right hand should embrace me.

tcz: Vo Jerusalem chanute, kijoldeina kiti hi aphat didol tah alhin kahsea nanghon kaithoulou ding in kitem uvin.
en_web: I adjure you, daughters of Jerusalem, that you not stir up, nor awaken love, until it so desires.
en_kjv: I charge you, O daughters of Jerusalem, That ye stir not up, nor awake my love, until he please.

tcz: Zailom: Gamthip’a kon hungpheija, agoldei chunga kingailha khu koi hija? Ka hin thoukhang tai hiche theithup phungnoi, na chunnun nahin pensahna, sonat na hin thohpi na mun’a chun.
en_web: Who is this who comes up from the wilderness, leaning on her beloved? Under the apple tree I awakened you. There your mother conceived you. There she was in labor and bore you.
en_kjv: Who is this that cometh up from the wilderness, Leaning upon her beloved? I raised thee up under the apple tree: There thy mother brought thee forth: There she brought thee forth that bare thee.

tcz: Mounu: Na-anglaija Mohor (Namdet melchih) kinam bang in neikoi jin, ajeh chu ngailutna hi thina toh kibanga thahattah ahin, kideina-a kon kithangsetna hi lhankhuh sunga ki um’a kithohgim tobang ahi. Kigoldeina hi meikong banga deo jejua, chule meikong lah-a akoupen tobang ahi.
en_web: Set me as a seal on your heart, as a seal on your arm; for love is strong as death. Jealousy is as cruel as Sheol. Its flashes are flashes of fire, a very flame of the LORD.
en_kjv: Set me as a seal upon thine heart, As a seal upon thine arm: For love is strong as death; Jealousy is cruel as the grave: The coals thereof are coals of fire, Which hath a most vehement flame.

tcz: Kingailutna hi twi ijat in jong achap mit joupon, vadung hon jong alhohmit joulou ahi. Khat touvin ngailutna hi anei-agou jousen chohtho ding gotaleh, alunggot chu imacha hidehlou ding ahi.
en_web: Many waters can’t quench love, neither can floods drown it. If a man would give all the wealth of his house for love, he would be utterly scorned.
en_kjv: Many waters cannot quench love, Neither can the floods drown it: If a man would give all the substance of his house for love, It would utterly be contemned.

tcz: Zailom: Keihon sopi numei kumdong, a-ang jong bohdoh nailou khat kanei jui. Khat touvin chongmou din thumna hung nei taleh, ka sopinu’u dinga ipi ka bolpeh thei diu ham?
en_web: We have a little sister. She has no breasts. What shall we do for our sister in the day when she is to be spoken for?
en_kjv: We have a little sister, and she hath no breasts: What shall we do for our sister in the day when she shall be spoken for?

tcz: Ama hi pal banga ding jangpet nungah theng ahileh, gal panmun sang dangka-a ka sem uva ka venbit diu ahi. Hinlah ama chu kotkha kikaile-kisonle banga detna neilou khat ahileh, ama venna dinga Cedar thinga pal kakam diu ahi.
en_web: If she is a wall, we will build on her a turret of silver. If she is a door, we will enclose her with boards of cedar.
en_kjv: If she be a wall, we will build upon her a palace of silver: And if she be a door, we will inclose her with boards of cedar.

tcz: Mounu: Keima pal banga ding jang nungah theng chu kana hi-e, tuhin ka-ang teni hi insang kisa inting vum abang’e. Ka goldeipan eihin vet teng, ka chunga athilmu chung ah alunglhai ngeije.
en_web: I am a wall, and my breasts like towers, then I was in his eyes like one who found peace.
en_kjv: I am a wall, and my breasts like towers: Then was I in his eyes as one that found favour.

tcz: Solomon in Baal-hamon ah lengpilei aneiyin, hichu lou natongho asansah-in, amaho jouse chun atheiga man dingin dangka sangkhat apecheh-uve.
en_web: Solomon had a vineyard at Baal Hamon. He leased out the vineyard to keepers. Each was to bring a thousand shekels of silver for its fruit.
en_kjv: Solomon had a vineyard at Baal-hamon; He let out the vineyard unto keepers; Every one for the fruit thereof was to bring a thousand pieces of silver.

tcz: Hinlah keima lengpilei hi keija mong ahi in, keiman kapeh ding ahi. Solomon in dangka sangkhat eipeh angai poi. Hinla theiga ngah-a pangho vang dangka jani cheh kapeh ding ahi.
en_web: My own vineyard is before me. The thousand are for you, Solomon, two hundred for those who tend its fruit.
en_kjv: My vineyard, which is mine, is before me: Thou, O Solomon, must have a thousand, And those that keep the fruit thereof two hundred.

tcz: Moulang: Honleija cham jing, O ngainu, naloi ten nangma awgin ajah jeh-un avangphauve, keima jong nei jahsah-in.
en_web: You who dwell in the gardens, with friends in attendance, let me hear your voice!
en_kjv: Thou that dwellest in the gardens, The companions hearken to thy voice: Cause me to hear it.

tcz: Mounu: Hung in, O ka ngaipen pa! Muinam theiho pahna lhang chunga sapeng gol le sakhi chalgol bang in chom letan!
en_web: Come away, my beloved! Be like a gazelle or a young stag on the mountains of spices!
en_kjv: Make haste, my beloved, And be thou like to a roe or to a young hart Upon the mountains of spices.

tcz: Amoz chapa Isaiah-in Juda lengho Uziah, Jotham, Ahaz leh Hezekiah phat laiya Judah le Jerusalem chungchang gaova thil amuho:
en_web: The vision of Isaiah the son of Amoz, which he saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem, in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah.
en_kjv: The vision of Isaiah the son of Amoz, which he saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah.

tcz: Vanho ngaiyun! leisetnin phaten ngaiyun! Pakaiyin asei chu hiche hi ahi: “Kahin vahkhang leh kahin seiletsah chaten kachungah nachonseuvin neidou tauve.
en_web: Hear, heavens, and listen, earth; for the LORD has spoken: “I have nourished and brought up children and they have rebelled against me.
en_kjv: Hear, O heavens, and give ear, O earth: For the Lord hath spoken, I have nourished and brought up children, And they have rebelled against me.

tcz: Bongchal jengin jong apupa akihetnin, chule Sanganin jong apu’n apehna kong akihetnin, ahinlah kamiten vang amaho kahin vahkhang dan ahephapouvin, Israelin apupa akihettapoi.
en_web: The ox knows his owner, and the donkey his master’s crib; but Israel doesn’t know. My people don’t consider.”
en_kjv: The ox knoweth his owner, And the ass his master’s crib: But Israel doth not know, My people doth not consider.

tcz: Ohe themmona dimsette chonse nam mite, gitlouna thilbol chilhahho; themmona dimset mite, hiche mite hin a-Pakaiyu adalhatauvin, Israel Mithengpa chu donselouvin akoiyun ajamsan tauve.
en_web: Ah sinful nation, a people loaded with iniquity, offspring of evildoers, children who deal corruptly! They have forsaken the LORD. They have despised the Holy One of Israel. They are estranged and backward.
en_kjv: Ah sinful nation, a people laden with iniquity, A seed of evildoers, children that are corrupters: They have forsaken the Lord, They have provoked the Holy One of Israel unto anger, They are gone away backward.

tcz: Ipi dinga gimbolna ding nakikou bebeu hitam? Itih chan gei neidou nahlai diu ham? naluchang apumin anatan, nalungchang jong ana’n ahi.
en_web: Why should you be beaten more, that you revolt more and more? The whole head is sick, and the whole heart faint.
en_kjv: Why should ye be stricken any more? Ye will revolt more and more: The whole head is sick, and the whole heart faint.

tcz: Nakengtoa pat nalujang chan adam lai mong mong aumtapon, akita-dupna jeng, apat lai jeng chule athi lonna maha jeng ahi’n, anaikolin, tom jong akitompon, thao jong akinupoi.
en_web: From the sole of the foot even to the head there is no soundness in it, but wounds, welts, and open sores. They haven’t been closed, bandaged, or soothed with oil.
en_kjv: From the sole of the foot even unto the head there is no soundness in it; But wounds, and bruises, and putrifying sores: They have not been closed, neither bound up, neither mollified with ointment.

tcz: Nagamsungu jong ahomkeovin alumtan, nakhopiu jong akavamtai. Namitmu tah'un gamdang miten nagam’u alosohtan, thil jouse amitmuva amu jouseu asusetauve.
en_web: Your country is desolate. Your cities are burned with fire. Strangers devour your land in your presence and it is desolate, as overthrown by strangers.
en_kjv: Your country is desolate, Your cities are burnt with fire: Your land, strangers devour it in your presence, And it is desolate, as overthrown by strangers.

tcz: Jerusalem khopi hoitah chu lengpi leiya buh kisong tobang leh changmai leiya buh kisong bangin, akidalhan avengbit ding umlou khopi abangtai.
en_web: The daughter of Zion is left like a shelter in a vineyard, like a hut in a field of melons, like a besieged city.
en_kjv: And the daughter of Zion is left as a cottage in a vineyard, As a lodge in a garden of cucumbers, As a besieged city.

tcz: Pakai van-khopi sepaihon eiho themkhat jeng jong eivenbitlouvu hileh Sodom le Gomorrah tobanga thehngima ium diu ahi.
en_web: Unless the LORD of Armies had left to us a very small remnant, we would have been as Sodom. We would have been like Gomorrah.
en_kjv: Except the Lord of hosts had left unto us a very small remnant, We should have been as Sodom, And we should have been like unto Gomorrah.

tcz: Sodom khoa vaihom lamkaihon Pakai thusei ngaiyun lang, Gomorrah miten Pathen dan thupeh ngaiyun.
en_web: Hear the LORD’s word, you rulers of Sodom! Listen to the law of our God, you people of Gomorrah!
en_kjv: Hear the word of the Lord, ye rulers of Sodom; Give ear unto the law of our God, ye people of Gomorrah.

tcz: Pakaiyin aseiye: “Nakilhainau jouseu hi ka-ipi phatchomna umdinga nagelluham? Keiman kelngoichal pumgo thilto le gancha kivah thaotahtah jong kaneiye. Keiman bongchal tampi thisan leh kelngoi thisan chule kelcha thisan hijongleh kakipapipoi.
en_web: “What are the multitude of your sacrifices to me?”, says the LORD. “I have had enough of the burnt offerings of rams and the fat of fed animals. I don’t delight in the blood of bulls, or of lambs, or of male goats.
en_kjv: To what purpose is the multitude of your sacrifices unto me? saith the Lord: I am full of the burnt offerings of rams, and the fat of fed beasts; And I delight not in the blood of bullocks, or of lambs, or of he goats.

tcz: Keima eihou dinga nahung tenguleh koiham nakithoinau puma ka-inpi chonthang dinga nakouvu?
en_web: When you come to appear before me, who has required this at your hand, to trample my courts?
en_kjv: When ye come to appear before me, Who hath required this at your hand, to tread my courts?

tcz: Pannabei thiltoho chu hinpolut tahih-un, nagimnamtuiyu jong keima dinga thet-umtah ahi! Lhathah nikho, Sabbath nikho chuleh achombeha na-anngol nikho manhou chonset bulom leh adihlou ahi. Nakikhopkhomnau jong kadeitapoi.
en_web: Bring no more vain offerings. Incense is an abomination to me. New moons, Sabbaths, and convocations— I can’t stand evil assemblies.
en_kjv: Bring no more vain oblations; incense is an abomination unto me; The new moons and sabbaths, the calling of assemblies, I cannot away with; It is iniquity, even the solemn meeting.

tcz: Nalhathah kut bolhou, kumlhun golnop nabolhou jong keidinga pohgih bep ahin, abonchan kapochimtan, kakidah ahitai!
en_web: My soul hates your New Moons and your appointed feasts. They are a burden to me. I am weary of bearing them.
en_kjv: Your new moons and your appointed feasts my soul hateth: They are a trouble unto me; I am weary to bear them.

tcz: Vanlam sanga nakhut-u natundohuva natao tengu jongleh kahungvetnuva nataonau kangailhahpehlou ding ahi. Ajeh chu khohelouho thisan nakhutnuvah adimsetne.
en_web: When you spread out your hands, I will hide my eyes from you. Yes, when you make many prayers, I will not hear. Your hands are full of blood.
en_kjv: And when ye spread forth your hands, I will hide mine eyes from you: Yea, when ye make many prayers, I will not hear: Your hands are full of blood.

tcz: Nangho kisilngimuvin lang chule kisuthengun! Nachonset nau chu kamitmun paimangun, nachonset nau lampi chu dalhauvin,
en_web: Wash yourselves. Make yourself clean. Put away the evil of your doings from before my eyes. Cease to do evil.
en_kjv: Wash ye, make you clean; put away the evil of your doings from before mine eyes;

tcz: Thilphabol dan kithemchuh-un, thudih chu holun. Bolgentheina thoh ho chu panpiuvin, naochagaho chu thu adih-in tanpeh-uvin lang, vengphauvin. Meithaiho chu thildih jeng seipeh-un.”
en_web: Learn to do well. Seek justice. Relieve the oppressed. Defend the fatherless. Plead for the widow.”
en_kjv: Cease to do evil; learn to do well; Seek judgment, relieve the oppressed, Judge the fatherless, plead for the widow.

tcz: Pakaiyin hiti hin aseiye, “Hungun kihoutoh-u hite. Nachonset nau chu thisan bangin san jongleh buhbang banga kabansah ding, sandup jeju jongleh kelngoi mul jolsel tobanga kajolsah ding ahi.
en_web: “Come now, and let’s reason together,” says the LORD: “Though your sins are as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow. Though they are red like crimson, they shall be as wool.
en_kjv: Come now, and let us reason together, saith the Lord: Though your sins be as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow; Though they be red like crimson, they shall be as wool.

tcz: Kathupeh nanit-uleh nanghon nehlechah ninglhingset’na nanei diu ahi.
en_web: If you are willing and obedient, you will eat the good of the land;
en_kjv: If ye be willing and obedient, ye shall eat the good of the land:

tcz: Ahinlah kathupeh nanitlou-uva nakiheimangsanule namelmateu chemjama lousoh helding nahiuve, tia na-Pakaiyu keiman kaseipeh nahitauve!”
en_web: but if you refuse and rebel, you will be devoured with the sword; for the LORD’s mouth has spoken it.”
en_kjv: But if ye refuse and rebel, Ye shall be devoured with the sword: For the mouth of the Lord hath spoken it.

tcz: I-atileh Jerusalem khopi kitahtah chu notia pang jenga hitam? Thu adih-a kitanna khopia chun tuhin tolthana jengin aumtai.
en_web: How the faithful city has become a prostitute! She was full of justice. Righteousness lodged in her, but now there are murderers.
en_kjv: How is the faithful city become a harlot! It was full of judgment; righteousness lodged in it; But now murderers.

tcz: Nadangka thih chu twieh asohgamtan, nalengpi twi chihtah chu twi toh akichohhal gamtai.
en_web: Your silver has become dross, your wine mixed with water.
en_kjv: Thy silver is become dross, Thy wine mixt with water:

tcz: Namilen milalteu jong doumahmah bolin apangun, gucha michomho jol le golin apang tauve. Nehguh chahguh adelleleuvin, nulou palouho thule meithaiho thujong adih-in atanpeh nom tapouve.
en_web: Your princes are rebellious and companions of thieves. Everyone loves bribes and follows after rewards. They don’t defend the fatherless, neither does the cause of the widow come to them.
en_kjv: Thy princes are rebellious, and companions of thieves: Every one loveth gifts, and followeth after rewards: They judge not the fatherless, Neither doth the cause of the widow come unto them.

tcz: Hijehchun Pakai, vantil galsatte Pakai Hatchungnung, Israel Pakai chun aseiye, “Keiman kamelmate chunga phuba kalah ding ahi.
en_web: Therefore the Lord, GOD of Armies, the Mighty One of Israel, says: “Ah, I will get relief from my adversaries, and avenge myself on my enemies.
en_kjv: Therefore saith the Lord, the Lord of hosts, the mighty One of Israel, Ah, I will ease me of mine adversaries, And avenge me of mine enemies:

tcz: Nachunga kakhut kalha ding, nathih-eh thengsella kathehngima nasum kilhajol chengse kaloikhensohkei ding ahi.
en_web: I will turn my hand on you, thoroughly purge away your dross, and will take away all your tin.
en_kjv: And I will turn my hand upon thee, And purely purge away thy dross, And take away all thy tin:

tcz: Chutengleh thutan vaihomthemho masang banga kahinpeh kit ding, Jerusalem khopi chu Thudih-a Kivaihomna Khopi chule Khopi Kitah tia kisei kit ding ahitai,” ati.
en_web: I will restore your judges as at the first, and your counselors as at the beginning. Afterward you shall be called ‘The city of righteousness, a faithful town.’
en_kjv: And I will restore thy judges as at the first, And thy counsellers as at the beginning: Afterward thou shalt be called, The city of righteousness, the faithful city.

tcz: Zion chu thudih-a akitan teng kiledoh kit ding chule akisihho chu chonphatnaa kiledoh kit diu ahitai.
en_web: Zion shall be redeemed with justice, and her converts with righteousness.
en_kjv: Zion shall be redeemed with judgment, And her converts with righteousness.

tcz: Michonseho vang suhmanga umding ahiuve, ijeh-inem itileh amaho Pakai hengah akile nompouve.
en_web: But the destruction of transgressors and sinners shall be together, and those who forsake the LORD shall be consumed.
en_kjv: And the destruction of the transgressors and of the sinners shall be together, And they that forsake the Lord shall be consumed.

tcz: Namilim hounau leh aguh-a gangpithing noi laha nachonnau leh milim houna'a nakipehdohnau jeh'a jumleja nathoh diu ahi.
en_web: For they shall be ashamed of the oaks which you have desired, and you shall be confounded for the gardens that you have chosen.
en_kjv: For they shall be ashamed of the oaks which ye have desired, And ye shall be confounded for the gardens that ye have chosen.

tcz: Anagopsa gangpi phung nabah diu, chule twilutlouna honlei toh nabah diu ahi.
en_web: For you shall be as an oak whose leaf fades, and as a garden that has no water.
en_kjv: For ye shall be as an oak whose leaf fadeth, And as a garden that hath no water.

tcz: Nalahuva ahatpenpa jong chu changpol tobanga mangthah ding; athilbol dihlouhou chu meisipah mei chohkaiya pang ding, amaho le athildihlou bolhou chu meikong lah-a kachaiyintin, chuleh meikong chu aphelmit thei ding koima umponte.
en_web: The strong will be like tinder, and his work like a spark. They will both burn together, and no one will quench them.”
en_kjv: And the strong shall be as tow, And the maker of it as a spark, And they shall both burn together, and none shall quench them.

tcz: Hiche hi Amoz chapa Isaiah-in Judah le Jerusalem chungchanga mu anei chu ahi.
en_web: This is what Isaiah the son of Amoz saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem.
en_kjv: The word that Isaiah the son of Amoz saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem.

tcz: Ninunung lam tengleh Pakai molsang chu molsang jouse sanga achungnungpen’a hung kitungdoh ding ahi’n, hicheteng chuleh namtin vaipi jouse hiche molsang chunga chu hungkhom diu ahi.
en_web: It shall happen in the latter days, that the mountain of the LORD’s house shall be established on the top of the mountains, and shall be raised above the hills; and all nations shall flow to it.
en_kjv: And it shall come to pass in the last days, That the mountain of the Lord’s house shall be established in the top of the mountains, And shall be exalted above the hills; And all nations shall flow unto it.

tcz: Namtin vaipi hungkhom diu chule hitia hi aseidiu ahi: “Hungun gakaltou-u hite Pakai molsang, Jacob Pathen in'ah; chuteng Ama’n Ama lampi dih chu eihil diu, Ama lampi dih-a chu lam ijotthei diu ahi. Ajeh chu Zion’a kon’a Pakai danthu hung potdoh ding Jerusalema kon’a Pakai thusei hung potdoh ding ahi.
en_web: Many peoples shall go and say, “Come, let’s go up to the mountain of the LORD, to the house of the God of Jacob; and he will teach us of his ways, and we will walk in his paths.” For the law shall go out of Zion, and the LORD’s word from Jerusalem.
en_kjv: And many people shall go and say, Come ye, and let us go up to the mountain of the Lord, To the house of the God of Jacob; And he will teach us of his ways, And we will walk in his paths: For out of Zion shall go forth the law, And the word of the Lord from Jerusalem.

tcz: Pakai chun namtin vaipi kah-a thudih-a thu ahin tanding chule chitin namtin dinga thutanlhahna ahin nei ding, mihon achamjem’u tuchaa akikhen diu, atengchau jong kangkuiya akikhen diu, chutengle nam khatnin nam khat dounaa hem le thal alaplou heldiu ahitai. Chule galbol ding dan kihilna umtalou ding ahi.
en_web: He will judge between the nations, and will decide concerning many peoples. They shall beat their swords into plowshares, and their spears into pruning hooks. Nation shall not lift up sword against nation, neither shall they learn war any more.
en_kjv: And he shall judge among the nations, And shall rebuke many people: And they shall beat their swords into plowshares, And their spears into pruninghooks: Nation shall not lift up sword against nation, Neither shall they learn war any more.
